neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/index.title: Adventuring Gear
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/index.content: Common gear used for adventuring in the Stardust Rhapsody

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/ammunition.title: Ammunition
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/ammunition.content:
Ammunition is required by a weapon that has the Ammunition property. A weapon’s description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon. The Ammunition table lists the different types and the amount you get when you buy them. The table also lists the item that is typically used to store each type; storage must be bought separately.

Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/amplifier.title: Amplifier
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/amplifier.content:
An Amplifier is a speaker that amplifies sounds so they can be heard up to 300 feet away. It comes with a hand-held microphone, and can be paired with a Communicator, a data storage device for playing audio files, or a Musician’s Instrument.
Cost: 500 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/ascension-.title: Ascension Gun
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/ascension-.content:
An Ascension Gun is a compact device with a high-strength cable and anchoring head fired by gas or magnetic acceleration. As a Utilize action, you can fire the gun at a surface or object you can see within 100 feet of yourself, and the head anchors if you succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. As part of the same action, or as a Bonus Action on subsequent turns, you can retract the cable 25 feet, hauling up to 500 pounds toward the anchor point, or a weight lighter than you and no more than 500 pounds toward yourself.
Cost: 2,000 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/camera.title: Camera
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/camera.content:
A Camera can take still pictures or record video and audio. It stores recorded media on a removable Data Chip.
Cost: 500 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/canteen.title: Canteen
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/canteen.content:
A Canteen holds up to a half gallon. If you don’t drink sufficient water, you risk dehydration (see the D&D Beyond Basic Rules).
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/case,-shel.title: Case, Shell
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/case,-shel.content:
A Shell Case holds up to 10 Shells.
Cost: 50 GN
Case
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/climbing-k.title: Climbing Kit
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/climbing-k.content:
A Climbing Kit includes boot tips, gloves, pitons, and a harness. As a Utilize action, you can use the Climber’s Kit to anchor yourself; when you do, you can’t fall more than 25 feet from the anchor point, and you can’t move more than 25 feet from there without undoing the anchor as a Bonus Action.
Cost: 1,250 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/clothing,-.title: Clothing, Designer
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/clothing,-.content:
Designer Clothes are made of expensive fabrics and adorned with expertly crafted details. Some events and locations admit only people wearing these clothes.
Cost: 750 GN
Clothing
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/clothing,-.title: Clothing, Traveling
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/clothing,-.content:
Traveling Clothes are resilient garments designed for travel in various environments.
Cost: 100 GN
Clothing
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/clothing.title: Clothing
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/clothing.content:

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/communicat.title: Communicator, High Power
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/communicat.content:
A High Power Communicator includes a backpack power and central unit with a compact antenna, and a headset or hand transceiver. It can also be easily mounted in a vehicle. A High Power Communicator can connect to a communication network, or it can directly connect to another comm device in a range up to 25 miles with direct line of sight. It can store comm codes or select frequencies. If you use the comm in an area of jamming, if you succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence (Computers) check, the comm functions until the start of your next turn. A Power Cell powers the unit for 24 hours of use.
If you aren’t maintaining a Lifestyle, the communicator can’t connect to a comm network.
Cost: 15,000 GN
Communicator
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/communicat.title: Communicator, Personal
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/communicat.content:
A Personal Communicator is a Tiny device easily held in the palm of one hand. It can connect to a communication network to allow long distance calling or directly connect to another comm device over a short range—1 mile with direct line of sight, or 1,000 feet in a city or similar terrain. It has its own unique comm code and can store hundreds of codes for easy calling. The communicator functions for 48 hours before needing to be recharged (1 hour connected to a power source).
If you aren’t maintaining a Lifestyle, the communicator can’t connect to a comm network.
Cost: 1,500 GN
Communicator
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/communicat.content:

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/cord.title: Cord
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/cord.content:
Cord is 10 feet long. You can tie a knot in it as a Utilize action.
Cost: 5 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/cosmic-sym.title: Cosmic Symbol
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/cosmic-sym.content:
A Cosmic Symbol takes one of the forms in the Cosmic Symbol table and is machined or inscribed to channel cosmic magic. An Enforcer or Oracle can use a Cosmic Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus.
The table indicates whether a Cosmic Symbol needs to be held, worn, or born on fabric (such as clothing or a banner) or a suit of armor or a Shield.

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/data-chip.title: Data Chip
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/data-chip.content:
A Data Chip is a digital storage unit easily held in the palm of a hand. You can insert the chip into Datapads, computers, or other devices to access, transfer, and store information. A standard Data Chip can store 4,000 pages of simple, text-only data—about 100 books worth. The same device can hold 400 photos or other still images, 200 hours of audio, 48 hours of high-definition video, or 3 high complexity computer programs.
Cost: 125 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/datapad.title: Datapad
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/datapad.content:
A Datapad is a device that stores data in the form of text, audio, or video files, has simple audio-video recording capability, and can execute simple programs. If you consult an accurate nonfiction Datapad file about its topic, you gain a +5 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana, Computers, History, Nature, Religion, or Technology) checks you make about that topic. The pad’s information is stored on a removable Data Chip (included with a newly purchased or crafted Datapad).
Cost: 1,250 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/disguise.title: Disguise
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/disguise.content:
While wearing a Disguise, you have Advantage on any ability check you make to impersonate the person or type of person it represents.
Cost: 250 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/flamethrow.title: Flamethrower
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/flamethrow.content:
A Flamethrower is a pistol-like device with a pressure nozzle and an igniter beneath it. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with firing the Flamethrower. Each creature in a 15-foot Cone must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d4 Fire damage. Flammable objects in the Cone that aren’t being worn or carried begin burning (see the D&D Beyond Free Rules). After three uses, you must reload the Flamethrower with a Fuel Oil flask as an action or a Bonus Action.
Cost: 2,000 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/flashlight.title: Flashlight
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/flashlight.content:
A Flashlight is a handheld device that uses a Power Cell to produce light. You can turn the light on or off (no action required) once during your turn. A Power Cell powers a Flashlight for 10 hours of use.
The Flashlight has three modes, which you can switch as a Bonus Action.
Ambient. The light produces Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet.
Spotlight. The light produces Bright Light in a 60-foot Cone and Dim Light for an additional 60 feet.
Subtle. The light produces Dim Light in a 5-foot radius.
Cost: 25 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/grapnel.title: Grapnel
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/grapnel.content:
As a Utilize action, you can throw the Grapnel at a railing, a ledge, or another catch within 50 feet of yourself, and the hook catches on if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. If you tied a Synth Line to the hook, you can then climb it.
Cost: 100 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/grav-spike.title: Grav Spikes
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/grav-spike.content:
As a Utilize action, you can spread Grav Spikes to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 1 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Grav Spikes.
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/healing-st.title: Healing Stim
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/healing-st.content:
A Healing Stim is a hypertech version of a Potion of Healing. This injector, medicine elixir, or dermal patch is a magic item. As a Bonus Action, you can administer it to yourself or another creature within 5 feet of you. The target regains 2d4 + 2 Hit Points.
Cost: 2,500 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/holoprojec.title: Holoprojector
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/holoprojec.content:
A Holoprojector is a compact, portable holo emitter with limited storage, about the size of a deck of cards. You can activate or deactivate it with a Utilize action, and you can select a new stored image as part of the same action. While activated, it projects a holographic image up to 5 feet away from it. The projector can store up to 10 images. An image can be an object, a creature, or a scene such as a photograph, and it can be animated with one round worth of movement or apparent actions, which can loop. The projector has enough power to operate for 10 minutes before needing to be recharged (which takes 1 hour connected to a power source), or it can be wired into a power source for continuous function.
Physical contact reveals the hologram for what it is. A creature can take the Study action to examine the image, and determines its true nature with a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check.
Cost: 1,000 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/igniter.title: Igniter
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/igniter.content:
An Igniter is a small device that uses sparks and simple fuel to create a small flame. Using it to light a candle or anything with exposed fuel or constructed of flammable material takes a Bonus Action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.
Cost: 5 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/intruder's.title: Intruder's Pack
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/intruder's.content:
An Intruder’s Pack contains the following items: Rucksack (matte black or gray), Canteen, Flashlight, Grapnel, Igniter, Motion Sensor, Power Cell, Pry Bar, 5 Ration Pouches, Steel Bearings, Synth Line.
Cost: 755 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/link-cable.title: Link Cable
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/link-cable.content:
A 20-foot spool of cable with connectors at each end for transferring power or data.
Cost: 15 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/macro-scop.title: Macro Scope
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/macro-scop.content:
A Macro Scope is an optical enhancer for viewing distant things. Standard, commercially available models allow detailed viewing out to double a user’s normal sight range. More expensive variant models add different functionality, such as longer range or vision modes.
As a Utilize action, you can fit a scope to a ranged weapon with the Two-Handed property. Ranged attack rolls with the weapon don’t have Disadvantage for firing at a target beyond close range if you don’t move during the same turn.
Cost: 2,500 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/medic's-ki.title: Medic's Kit
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/medic's-ki.content:
A Medic’s Kit has ten uses. As a Utilize action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an Unconscious creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.
Cost: 250 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/motion-sen.title: Motion Sensor
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/motion-sen.content:
A Tiny device that detects movement within 5 feet of its front. You can activate or deactivate it as a Utilize action, and it has an adhesive pad on the back that allows it to be affixed to a surface as part of the same action. While activated, when a Small or larger creature or object moves within 5 feet of the sensor’s front, it emits a sound that can be heard up to 60 feet away. It can operate for 24 hours before needing to be recharged (which takes 1 hour connected to a power source), or it can be wired into a power source for continuous function.
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/night-visi.title: Night Vision Goggles
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/night-visi.content:
These goggles enhance existing light and use infrared light sources to provide you with Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. The goggles require a Power Cell (included) and function for 8 hours on a full cell.
Cost: 3,500 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/outrunner'.title: Outrunner's Pack
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/outrunner'.content:
An Outrunner’s Pack contains the following items: Rucksack, Canteen, Flashlight, Grav Spikes, Igniter, Power Cell, Pry Bar, 10 Ration Pouches, Synth Line.
Cost: 730 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/performer'.title: Performer's Pack
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/performer'.content:
A Performer’s Pack contains the following items: Rucksack, Amplifier, Camera, Canteen, Data Chip, 3 Disguises, Flashlight, Igniter, Motion Sensor, Power Cell, 10 Ration Pouches, Sleeping Bag.
Cost: 655 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/power-cell.title: Power Cell
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/power-cell.content:
Power Cells are compact energy storage devices compatible with a wide spectrum of equipment. A standard Power Cell can’t be recharged.
Energy Weapons. A Power Cell powers a ranged weapon that uses it for ammunition or a powered melee weapon. The weapons’ properties list how many shots or attacks a cell can power.
Powered Devices. The description of a piece of equipment that requires a Power Cell for power notes how long the cell can power it. Changing a Power Cell in a device requires either an action or Bonus Action.
Cost: 100 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/primal-foc.title: Primal Focus
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/primal-foc.content:
A Primal Focus takes one of the forms in the Primal Focuses table and is carved, chiseled, or painted to channel primal magic. A Primalist or Tracer can use such an object as a Spellcasting Focus.
Primal Focuses

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/pry-bar.title: Pry Bar
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/pry-bar.content:
Using a Pry Bar gives you Advantage on Strength checks where the Pry Bar’s leverage can be applied.
Cost: 100 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/ration-pou.title: Ration Pouch
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/ration-pou.content:
Ration Packs consist of travel-ready food, including dried meat and fruit, dense bread, nuts, and shelf stable pouches or hard containers. See “Malnutrition” in the D&D Beyond Basic Rules for the risks of not eating.
Cost: 25 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/rucksack.title: Rucksack
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/rucksack.content:
A Rucksack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag for a mount, or a motorcycle or similar vehicle.
Cost: 100 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/silencer.title: Silencer
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/silencer.content:
A Silencer is a device that dissipates escaping propellant gases when fitted to the muzzle of a Ranged weapon that fires Bullets and has a damage die of 1d8 or smaller. You can attach or remove a Silencer with a Utilize action. A listener within 30 feet of a silenced gunshot hears the muffled shot with a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check.
A weapon with a Silencer attached has its range halved.
Cost: 500 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/sleeping-b.title: Sleeping Bag
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/sleeping-b.content:
A Sleeping Bag sleeps one Small or Medium creature. While in a Sleeping Bag, you automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold (see the D&D Beyond Basic Rules).
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/steel-bear.title: Steel Bearings
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/steel-bear.content:
As a Utilize action, you can spill Steel Bearings from their pouch. They spread to cover a level, 10-foot-square area within 10 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Steel Bearings.
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/synth-line.title: Synth Line
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/synth-line.content:
A 50-foot length of synthetic fiber rope. As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Synth Line if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The Synth Line can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.
You can bind an unwilling creature with the Synth Line only if the creature has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition. If the creature’s legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Synth Line requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Athletics) check as an action.
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/technician.title: Technician's Pack
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/technician.content:
A Technician’s Pack contains the following items: Rucksack, Cord, Datapad (technical schematic), Flashlight, Igniter, Link Cable, 2 Power Cells, Pry Bar, 5 Ration Pouches, Synth Line, Thermal Blanket
Cost: 1,880 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/thermal-bl.title: Thermal Blanket
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/thermal-bl.content:
A waterproof, reflective blanket also useful as a drop cloth or tarp. While wrapped in a Thermal Blanket, you have Advantage on saving throws against extreme cold (see the D&D Beyond Free Rules).
Cost: 5 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/trench-coa.title: Trench Coat
neon-odyssey/adventuring-gear/trench-coa.content:
A Trench Coat is a practical or vocational garment. It is waterproof, has many pockets, and can conceal larger carried objects.
Cost: 50 GN
Adventuring Gear

neon-odyssey/aether.title: Aether
neon-odyssey/aether.content:
Outer space in the Stardust Rhapsody is far from empty. It is filled with colorful clouds, nebulae, and currents of aether—a breathable gas that conducts heat much like a world’s atmosphere. While a creature can survive in it, aether is far from safe. Prolonged exposure saturates a creature with the strange energies aether carries, breaking down biological and living mechanical systems.
A creature breathing aether has the Poisoned condition. It must also make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw after each hour of exposure. On a failed save, the creature gains 1 Exhaustion level and can’t remove Exhaustion until it spends 1 hour in an aether-free environment.
A creature with an air supply (or that doesn’t breathe) but that is otherwise exposed to the aether, such as one using a Breath Mask but without an Enviro Suit, isn’t Poisoned by the aether and makes the save every 8 hours instead.
Space and Aether

neon-odyssey/creatures/aberration.title: Aberration
neon-odyssey/creatures/aberration.content:
Entities that are from outside or existed before the Stardust Rhapsody and are typically totally strange to the galaxy. The Deep and other creatures of the Abyssal Void, the extra-dimensional Vort, and the Eldest are all Aberrations.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/beast.title: Beast
neon-odyssey/creatures/beast.content:
All manner of real-world animals exist in the galaxy. Sometimes they look mundane, but most typically they might be strangely colored or have biological adaptations to the world they inhabit. Neon Odyssey provides new adaptations to build your own Beasts with existing D&D stat blocks.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/celestial.title: Celestial
neon-odyssey/creatures/celestial.content:
Beings that are of mystic origin from the first song of creation are considered Celestials, which typically manifest in two varieties. There are the stellar entities of Agathos including the twelve gods and those who serve them, as well as the masked kindred and spirits of the Harmony, representing both Vital and Somber aspects.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/construct.title: Construct
neon-odyssey/creatures/construct.content:
Living things that are synthetic or built. Constructs are most commonly mechanical robots made from physical hardware or entirely digital beings from the Hypergrid made of code, sometimes with bodies of hard light.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/index.title: Creatures
neon-odyssey/creatures/index.content:
There are a wide variety of creatures that inhabit the Stardust Rhapsody and the cosmic realms beyond it. Every creature type of D&D is present in the galaxy, with a specific approach to ensure that they all fit in a Space Opera setting, some more changed than others. Knowing how creatures are represented will allow you to create your own bestiary to populate your campaign.

neon-odyssey/creatures/dragon.title: Dragon
neon-odyssey/creatures/dragon.content:
Rare and powerful creatures said to be representatives of the Stardust Rhapsody itself as well as descendants of the mythic Stardust Dragon. Besides this progenitor, they are not capable of speech or sapient communication, but their vocalizations have a musical quality to them.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/elemental.title: Elemental
neon-odyssey/creatures/elemental.content:
Coalesced entities of the raw, untamed, and chaotic primordial energy that exploded into existence when the galaxy came into being. They typically are consumed by a singular strong emotion that defines their behavior. Nearly all world souls and their spawn are Elementals.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/fey.title: Fey
neon-odyssey/creatures/fey.content:
Whimsical creatures of pure imagination generated by the power of creative thought. Nearly all Fey are from Arcadia, having digital roots but wholly changed with imaginative magic into their own type of entity. They may appear to be made of pixels or polygons, or even like living drawings, toys, or an endless number of colorful and sometimes silly incarnations.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/fiend.title: Fiend
neon-odyssey/creatures/fiend.content:
Beings created through the malevolent corruption of cosmic energies, including mortal souls. Nearly all Fiends are the Discordant of Cacophony, which all possess an inherent wickedness, but the respective tones have differing and competing goals. Entropy and Progress favor order while Instinct and Thrill favor chaos.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/giant.title: Giant
neon-odyssey/creatures/giant.content:
Creatures that emerge at convergence points in the flow of Harmony where its lifegiving energy surges and mixes with the environment, growing to massive size. Certain species like the raizo, yaungu, and even humans are said to be the descendants of Giants.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/humanoid.title: Humanoid
neon-odyssey/creatures/humanoid.content:
Nearly all sapient, soul-having people of the galaxy with organic biology are considered Humanoids, even if there is influence or heritage from other creature types. Many of the NPC and people stat blocks included in Neon Odyssey are Humanoid.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/monstrosity.title: Monstrosity
neon-odyssey/creatures/monstrosity.content:
There are countless alien creatures that inhabit the numerous worlds across the galaxy. Monstrosities may even appear similar to certain animals, but have strange biology, a cosmic essence, radical adaptations, magical power, or anything else that makes them more than a simple Beast. Nearly all new bestial creatures in Neon Odyssey are Monstrosities.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/ooze.title: Ooze
neon-odyssey/creatures/ooze.content:
When the song of creation was first sung, there were pockets of potent primordial goo generated as the byproduct of creation. Slime that emerged from this soup with a will of its own, as well as their spawn, are considered Oozes. A newer phenomenon is the living pollution spawned through waste, runoff, and defilement of a primordial place mixed with prevalent magical and hypertech residue.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/plant.title: Plant
neon-odyssey/creatures/plant.content:
The galaxy is teeming with colorful, strange, and alien flora and fungus, which sometimes develop levels of sentience or even sapience. Anything with such an origin is considered a Plant.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/creatures/undead.title: Undead
neon-odyssey/creatures/undead.content:
Once living things that have had their body or soul completely severed from the Harmony, collectively known throughout the galaxy as the Silent. Usually such an abomination only occurs from foul magic, strange experiments, or some other cosmic catastrophe. Most become tortured, mindless husks, but a rare few retain their will.
Creatures

neon-odyssey/factions/argonauts.title: Argonauts
neon-odyssey/factions/argonauts.content:
The Argonauts are a decentralized mercenary organization that offers their services to those who cannot necessarily afford the likes of GrimCo or other expensive agencies, out of a genuine desire to make the galaxy a safer place. They have an optimistic outlook with a desire to explore the galaxy, doing heavy promotion bordering on propaganda to secure donations and new recruits while often leaving out the gory details of battle and the risk involved. They are known for producing the best starfighters and starpilots in the galaxy, with some even becoming interstellar celebrities.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/bloodfleet.title: Bloodfleet
neon-odyssey/factions/bloodfleet.content:
The Bloodfleet is a loose alliance of space pirates that follow a pirate’s code of fellowship and freedom among the numerous crews that terrorize the Aether currents across the galaxy. They are highly superstitious and practice all manner of strange habits and rituals to ensure fortune and safe passage through space, particularly blood sacrifice into the ramshackle engines of their ships. They give up a body part of their own to join and many take additional sacrifices of flesh from the victims they spare, all in hopes of achieving greater plunder and glory.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/cavalon-empire.title: Cavalon Empire
neon-odyssey/factions/cavalon-empire.content:
The Cavalon Empire is the faction that controls the most territory in the galaxy, having brought a great amount of security and stability to wilder reaches of space and providing safe and quick travel between worlds. Ruled by an empress who leads a court of noble houses, the empire expects its citizens to follow its more stringent laws and adopt imperial culture—which is centered around a knightly code of chivalry—although how closely it is followed varies wildly. They specialize in the construction and piloting of powerful mechs and maintain a naval dominance to expand the borders of the empire.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/chemtek-revolution.title: Chemtek Revolution
neon-odyssey/factions/chemtek-revolution.content:
The Chemtek Revolution is a galactic rebellious movement that seeks to tear down all of the oppressive power structures of the galaxy, from governments to corporations. They utilize unconventional chemical and cybernetic enhancements to give them an even playing field against their opponents and employ extreme tactics to advance their aims, not caring about collateral damage. In a galaxy with so many disenfranchised peoples, their message spreads like wildfire with bright colors and punk culture.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/church-of-karkosa.title: Church of Karkosa
neon-odyssey/factions/church-of-karkosa.content:
The Church of Karkosa is a zealous religious organization that advances the fastest growing faith in the galaxy. Rejecting the twelve of Agathos, they worship a thirteenth god, Karkosa, who encourages change and rapid evolution to a new state of being to survive the inevitable doom coming to the Stardust Rhapsody when the Void finally consumes the galaxy once more, returning it to the dark and the deep of how it was before the song of creation was sung. They employ strange, otherworldly biotech and mystic mutations in their faith to spread their message among the stars, while offering genuine charitable services and missionary opportunities for the galaxy’s downtrodden in the form of free clinics, food banks, shelters, and refugee relocation.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/index.title: Factions
neon-odyssey/factions/index.content:
The Stardust Rhapsody is a galaxy at war with interstellar factions vying for power and seeking to achieve their own goals. Every major faction can be joined or fought against by player characters.
Argonauts
Bloodfleet
Cavalon Empire
Chemtek Revolution
Church of Karkosa
Grimnir Company
Kuzai Syndicate
Nexus Consortium
Polaris Society
Saurok Dynasty
Solar Federation
Void Dominium

neon-odyssey/factions/grimnir-company.title: Grimnir Company
neon-odyssey/factions/grimnir-company.content:
The Grimnir Company, better known as GrimCo, is a galaxy-spanning military industrial complex, selling top-of-the-line mercenaries, weapons, transports, and other technology of war to the highest bidder. They follow a strict code of business and neutrality, finding distaste for the scheming and backstabbing culture of the Nexus Consortium, and they are employed by nearly every major galactic faction and government. Their proprietary gravtech and aether processing makes them incredibly valuable on any battlefield.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/kuzai-syndicate.title: Kuzai Syndicate
neon-odyssey/factions/kuzai-syndicate.content:
The Kuzai Syndicate is the biggest crime organization in the galaxy, choosing to get involved in legitimate businesses as a palatable front as they conduct their more nefarious operations from the shadows. They are bold enough to operate in the territory of every faction, even those with the most burdensome laws, unafraid of those who would try to stop them. They believe in loyalty above all else, and those who are initiated into the family receive mystical tattoos imbued with the power of the somber aspect of the Harmony.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/nexus-consortium.title: Nexus Consortium
neon-odyssey/factions/nexus-consortium.content:
The Nexus Consortium is a collection of the biggest interstellar mega-corporations in the galaxy that have joined together to achieve the shared goal of maximizing their collective profits. These companies have brought a tremendous amount of comfort and convenience to the Stardust Rhapsody, even effectively establishing the general galactic culture of consumerism that becomes increasingly reliant upon them. While there are numerous corporations in the consortium, a small handful sit at the top.

Nexus Financial: Finance, banking, investments, real estate.
Kyojin Energy Company: Power, fuel, energy of all varieties.
Jemini Group: Entertainment, music, film, gaming, restaurants, theme parks.
Khymera Bionetics: Bio-engineering, healthcare, food production, medicine.
I.V.O. Industries: Technology, robotics, construction, labor markets.
Interstellar News Network (INN): News, information, data, telecommunications.

Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/polaris-society.title: Polaris Society
neon-odyssey/factions/polaris-society.content:
The Polaris Society is a secret society with a public front as an organization of wealthy elites who meet for social networking and to discuss the most pressing issues of the day. However, their true hidden purpose is to manipulate galactic politics and major events to maintain a balance of power and move the Stardust Rhapsody in the direction they desire, which they believe to be the will of Agathos. They employ highly trained agents and strange, alien, or even occult technology and relics to operate as major players that few realize.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/saurok-dynasty.title: Saurok Dynasty
neon-odyssey/factions/saurok-dynasty.content:
The Saurok Dynasty is the oldest surviving faction, ruled by a triumvirate spread across three disconnected seats of power. They hold a special reverence for the Harmony and for dinosaurs that integrate into their daily lives. They alone possess the ability to utilize highly advanced Harmonyte gemtech, which grants them the unique ability to instantly teleport across vast distances. Having been pushed to the brink of collapse by internal strife and their war with the Cavalon Empire, they seek to reclaim their former glory.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/solar-federation.title: Solar Federation
neon-odyssey/factions/solar-federation.content:
The Solar Federation is a loose collection of relatively independent worlds that have joined together for economic and political security. They believe in the freedom of their citizens and the rights of the various member worlds to rule how they see fit. They hold an elevated view of achievement and advancement in industry, the arts, sciences, and other pursuits but also turn a blind eye to the creeping corporate interests that grow in federation space.
Factions

neon-odyssey/factions/void-dominium.title: Void Dominium
neon-odyssey/factions/void-dominium.content:
The Void Dominium is a mighty, otherworldly military that survives in the brutal conditions of the Wyrmways and strives to conquer the Stardust Rhapsody to create a strengthened and unified galaxy that can withstand any cosmic threat. Their culture revolves around creating bonds with fearsome void wyrms that they ride into battle to disintegrate those who oppose them. They are merciless but follow a strict code of honor, and their hierarchy is entirely a meritocracy that cares not where one came from as long as they have the strength and will to fight and survive.
Factions

neon-odyssey/galactic-bounty-guild.title: Galactic Bounty Guild
neon-odyssey/galactic-bounty-guild.content:
Because of the complications of interstellar politics, heated conflicts, and diplomatic tensions, bounty hunters are commonly used as independent bringers of justice that can operate throughout faction territory and across numerous worlds. These bounties are managed by the Galactic Bounty Guild (GBG), a neutral organization respected and utilized by nearly all factions. Bounty hunters who join the GBG receive a membership card and are able to rise through the ranks to unlock increasingly more lucrative and dangerous jobs.
Outrunners

neon-odyssey/outrunners.title: Outrunners
neon-odyssey/outrunners.content:
While the Stardust Rhapsody is filled with grand galactic factions, planetary governments, and interstellar organizations, many people chart their own course throughout the stars and make their way through the galaxy individually or in small groups. These wayfarers are called Outrunners, the setting’s equivalent to Adventurers.
Outrunners often turn to bounty hunting, but not all get into that line of work. They might become salvagers, mercenaries, explorers, xeno hunters, smugglers, transporters, relic hunters, pirates, investigators, crisis responders, or countless other jobs that keep them the masters of their own fate. Most player characters in Neon Odyssey are Outrunners.
Galactic Bounty Guild
Setting Primer

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/abyssa.title: Abyssal Void
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/abyssa.content:
Beyond the protective starlight of Agathos is the infinite expanse of the Abyssal Void, an eldritch, unknowable realm devoid of color. It is said that the Void is what existed before the galaxy was created when the song of creation was sung by the Eldest. Its existence is a complete anathema to the Stardust Rhapsody, and is a place of the dark and quiet. Its very existence bends the mind, both consuming and radiating potent psionic energy.
The Deep
The Wyrmways
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/agatho.title: Agathos
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/agatho.content:
The entirety of the Stardust Rhapsody is surrounded by Agathos, the divine realm of the stars and the gods. Like a shell to an egg, it serves as the barrier between the galaxy and the Abyssal Void beyond, protecting the song of creation from annihilation. In this setting, suns and stars are distinct concepts, and Agathos contains all of the stars that can be seen throughout the whole galaxy, allowing for consistent stellar navigation.
Agathos is the home of the twelve gods of Agathos and the divine Celestials that revere and serve them. These deities care only for their primary spheres of influence, with the concepts of good and evil not being a concern to them. They are divided into four triads with shared kinship and loose philosophical alignment, their territory and constellations existing in a quadrant of the galaxy. These triads and their respective gods are as follows.
Beacon Triad
The Beacon Triad is one of vibrance, whether of light, emotion, revelry, or victory and glory.

Alara the Lightbringer: Goddess of light, love, beauty, passion, art, joy, desire, suns, etc.
Myrmona the Paragon: Goddess of war, competition, valor, athleticism, battle, glory, strength, victory, etc.
Xavrius the Celebrant: God of revelry, excitement, trickery, fun, laughter, performance, etc.

Chronicle Triad
The Chronicle Triad governs knowledge and understanding, not only information itself but also the relationship of things to each other throughout space, time, and destiny.

Daeda the Codex: Goddess of knowledge, technology, magic, invention, language, secrets, innovation, etc.
Ourolon the Clockmaker: God of time, fate, destiny, patience, prophecy, causality, etc.
Pelogos the Navigator: God of travel, navigation, exploration, adventure, discovery, crossings, horizons, etc.

Fountain Triad
The Fountain Triad is the wellspring of the natural universe expressed in the primeval elements of nature, the wilds of flora and fauna, and the cycle of life, death, and rebirth.

Eriphones the Maelstrom: God of the elements, chaos, freedom, upheaval, rebellion, natural disasters, etc.
Garwynn the Wildfather: God of nature, the hunt, flora, fauna, the wild, growth, survival, instinct, etc.
Seph the Faceless: Goddess of life, death, cycles, balance, seasons, rebirth, beginnings, endings, etc.

Tower Triad
The Tower Triad is that of builders of order and community, both the gathering of friends, family and neighbors in societies or trade, and of law in those societies and in the fundamental structure of the cosmos.

Khorabos the Architect: God of order, space, gravity, building, law, geometry, etc.
Tykris the Dealer: Goddess of luck, fortune, wealth, commerce, risk, gambling, opportunity, etc.
Vestaya the Hearthmother: Goddess of civilization, community, family, peace, hospitality, diplomacy, etc.

Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/arcadi.title: Arcadia
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/arcadi.content:
Arcadia is a realm of whimsy, creativity, and imagination, having changed and split off from the Hypergrid once the dreams of sapient beings combined the digital with the imaginative. It is an arcade world of color and maximalism populated by Fey creatures made of pixels and polygons—though they are fully physical beings, not digital. The realm operates entirely on video game logic, with levels, stages, and worlds to clear, collectibles to collect, and bosses to defeat.
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/cacoph.title: Cacophony
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/cacoph.content:
Cacophony is a hellish realm of malevolent mockery that was first created when the possible evil in the hearts of sapient beings corrupted and split off from the Harmony like a tumor. It is a realm that by its nature seeks to twist life to reflect itself, especially favoring sapient beings with souls that can be corrupted until they join its endless legions.
Discordant
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/discor.title: Discordant
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/discor.content:
The native denizens of Cacophony are Fiends known as Discordant. While they can be manifested directly from the malicious energies of the hellish dimension, many are the result of mortal beings being corrupted and transformed through the unhealthy coping of their pain. There are four distinct groups of Discordant that are simultaneously unified and opposed, each determined by their tone of Cacophony.
Entropy
Instinct
Progress
Thrill
Cacophony

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/entrop.title: Entropy
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/entrop.content:
The tone of Entropy is one of cold and decay, with hordes of vampiric fiends and monsters that crave the life essence of mortal beings, devouring it until there is nothing left and only Undead husks remain. They reside in great castles and crypts of stone and metal, brooding on the emptiness that exists within all of them, always seeking new victims to drain to temporarily sate their endless craving.
Discordant

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/harmon.title: Harmony
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/harmon.content:
The Harmony is the cosmic force of life and death that flows through the galaxy and connects all living things. It is defined by its two primary aspects, the Vital side of life and the Somber side of death. It is the source of living souls, and serves as the Stardust Rhapsody’s primary afterlife, with every soul that lives and dies returning to the oneness of the Harmony, slowly losing the individuality it once had and assimilating to the collective whole like notes in a symphony.
However, there is an entire spirit world within the realm, where masked Celestials comprised of numerous souls dwell, performing duties to advance and preserve the cycle of life and death. Individuals can project their souls into this realm or discover ways to step into its landscapes that are mystic reflections of the galaxy proper.
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/hyperg.title: Hypergrid
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/hyperg.content:
The Hypergrid is a fully digital realm that overlays the galaxy, interfacing with all technology both mundane and magical. The code of the Hypergrid exists throughout all the Stardust Rhapsody and is responsible for the immediate technological advancements that peoples of the galaxy achieved as they came into being. Gridrunners can manipulate this code to alter reality and perform their technomancy.
The very surface level of the Hypergrid serves as a universal internet utilized by the entire galaxy via computers and other digital systems. However, those who delve deeper can find an entire digital world with living programs made of code and civilizations built from pure data. Travelers can venture into the Hypergrid via digital avatars or by digitizing their bodies.
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/instin.title: Instinct
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/instin.content:
The tone of Instinct is one of wrath and destruction, comprised of an infinite swarm of grotesque bugs that tear down and dissolve civilization wherever they find it. They spawn in huge, pulsing hives where countless crawlers emerge to join the tide of skittering consumption that can spread across entire worlds until nothing remains but ash, bone, and the brood.
Discordant

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/progre.title: Progress
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/progre.content:
The tone of Progress is one of relentless singlemindedness, with methodical legions of hellish machines obsessed with technological advancement. They terminate all enemies to their march and assimilate their defeated foes whole into their endless war machine. An invasion from the forces of Progress can be apocalyptic to any society that does not kneel.
Discordant

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/index.title: Realms of the Cosmos
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/index.content:
Although most people will spend their entire lives in the galaxy proper, there is existence beyond its confines. Grand, extra-dimensional realms of the cosmos exist outside the galaxy, all of which are sources of otherworldly power and magic. They are analogous to the inner and outer planes of existence in D&D.
Agathos
Abyssal Void
Hypergrid
Harmony
Cacophony
Arcadia
Setting Primer

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/the-de.filePath: Neon Odyssey/Realms of the Cosmos/The Deep.md
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/the-de.title: The Deep
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/the-de.content:
Within the Abyssal Void, the most numerous denizens are completely alien, unknowable Aberrations that appear like horrific deep-sea creatures from tiny to utterly colossal. Collectively called the Deep, they are driven by hunger to devour existence and annihilate everything within. However, there is no maliciousness or hate within them, just an otherworldly indifference and the desire to act according to their unnatural nature.
Abyssal Void

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/the-wy.filePath: Neon Odyssey/Realms of the Cosmos/The Wyrmways.md
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/the-wy.title: The Wyrmways
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/the-wy.content:
Although Agathos serves as a bulwark against the Abyssal Void, there is a vast and complex network of metaphysical tunnels bored through the Overtone from the Void to the Stardust Rhapsody, chewed through by eldritch dragons—the Void Wyrms. Known as the Wyrmways, these passages are filled with a mixture of aether and the essence of the Void where few things can survive. Portals to the Wyrmways open and close seemingly at random in the form of black holes.
Abyssal Void

neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/thrill.title: Thrill
neon-odyssey/realms-of-the-cosmos/thrill.content:
The tone of Thrill is one of madcap energy and equal parts pain and pleasure, with a cavalcade of twisted clowns and other Fiends fit for a hellish circus. They sow colorful chaos wherever they go, and their unhinged sadism is at the heart of all they do. They corrupt from within with the promise of excitement and hedonism, until they are prepared to welcome a newly transformed fool to join their parade.
Discordant

neon-odyssey/setting-primer.title: Setting Primer
neon-odyssey/setting-primer.content:
A brief overview of Neon Odyssey’s setting, the Stardust Rhapsody. It was created specifically for the playtest and will not appear in the books. Its purpose is to give helpful context in creating characters, building encounters, or planning campaigns. Everything contained within is subject to change.
Stardust Rhapsody
Space and Aether
