The Eldest
Technology and Economy
Outrunners
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/space-and-aether.title: Space and Aether
neon-odyssey/space-and-aether.content:
Space is vast, but it is not an empty vacuum. It is filled with a gaseous substance called aether (EE-ther), which serves as the “fifth element” or the stuff of existence. It is inherently tied to the forces of space and gravity, and it ultimately serves as a building block for nearly all physical matter. It’s breathable but toxic to most living and synthetic beings, and prolonged exposure leads to deterioration and death outside of creatures native to space. Being ejected into space without an environment-sealed suit doesn’t instantly kill you, but death is nearly assured if you don’t find some form of rescue.
While the Stardust Rhapsody is not the same scale as the real-world universe, the galaxy is still immense, and spacefaring requires faster-than-light (FTL) travel. There are a variety of methods to achieve FTL, but any starship can travel through aether currents with the appropriate navigation. While easily accessible, this is the slowest form of FTL travel, and getting across the galaxy takes weeks or even longer depending on how far a distance there is to travel, and the whim of the currents.
To travel between worlds in a matter of days or even hours, starships can travel between Liminal Rings, which serve as gates in and out of the Overtone, an ephemeral plane that is analogous to D&D’s Border Ethereal and allows for especially rapid travel. Most Liminal Rings throughout the galaxy are built and maintained by the Cavalon Empire, Solar Federation, and Nexus Consortium.
Setting Primer

neon-odyssey/species/aetheron.title: Aetheron
neon-odyssey/species/aetheron.content:
Aetheron (EE-ther-awn) are a resilient people made of the stuff of space itself, allowing them to manipulate their connection to gravity and resist the effects of aether exposure. They typically prefer to live in outer space, often residing in massive space stations or spending their days aboard starships.
Many aetheron believe that they were crafted by Khorabos the Architect from a proto form of aether that drifted through the cosmos as a crystalized rock. They often seek orderliness in their lives that matches the tenets of their god, and this sense of order seems to manifest around them innately.
They are relatively short, often stoutly built, and are heavier than their size would suggest. Their skin tones are usually muted with casts of dull gray, blue, or purple, but they often have vibrant streaks of aether hues in their hair.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-5 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Titan IX
As an Aetheron, you have these special traits.
Aetheric Lock. You have Advantage on D20 Tests to avoid or end the Prone condition, or to avoid being moved from your space.
Architect’s Blessing. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes a D20 Test with Advantage or Disadvantage, you can enforce cosmic order and cause the roll to have neither Advantage nor Disadvantage. Once you use this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Tireless Core. You have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Exhaustion condition. Additionally, when you gain Exhaustion, you can reduce the number of levels gained by 1. Once you use this trait to reduce an Exhaustion level, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Unyielding Density. When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d12 plus your Proficiency Bonus. The first time you deal damage before the end of your next turn, one target takes extra Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You can take this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/amanite.title: Amanite
neon-odyssey/species/amanite.content:
Amanites (A-muh-nite) are fungal folk who originated in marshes and bogs overgrown with tree-sized mushrooms and teeming with huge, voracious creatures. They have adapted to thrive in this treacherous environment, developing magical spores they harness to evade the predators that seek to devour them.
Despite the threats that surround them, many amanites laugh in the face of danger and possess a love of adventure and discovery, seeking out mysteries to solve and relics to unearth.
Amanites are a diminutive people who resemble bipedal humanoid mushrooms that can vary in a wide spectrum of colors, textures, and patterns reminiscent of a huge diversity of fungus. Most typically have rounded noses, feature caps on their heads, and can grow fungal tendrils that evoke hair.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Small (about 3-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Sethreen
As an Amanite, you have these special traits.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Fungal Resistance. You have Resistance to Acid damage and Poison damage.
Mycelium Senses. You have proficiency in the Perception, Stealth, or Survival skill.
Spore Casting. You can use any mushroom as a Spellcasting Focus, and you know the Acid Splash cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have the Jump spell prepared, and starting at character level 5, you always have the Enlarge/Reduce spell prepared. You can cast each spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast each spell in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).
Spore Puff. As a Bonus Action, you can take the Dash action. When you do so, you release a cloud of spores that makes your space Heavily Obscured until the end of the turn. You can see through the cloud. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/anitron.title: Anitron
neon-odyssey/species/anitron.content:
Anitrons (AN-ih-tron) are living robots with a hyperspark—a technological soul originating from the Hypergrid and infused with the Harmony’s life energy. Scholars debate whether the first hypersparks manifested spontaneously, or if some inventor gave the first anitron their synthetic spirit.
Their mechanical bodies are each designed for a singular specialty in which they excel and often fixate on executing through free will instead of programmatic dictate.
Constructed from various materials and fashioned into a wide variety of body shapes and sizes, anitrons are one of the most physically diverse species in the galaxy.
Creature Type: Construct
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Megadyne
As an Anitron, you have these special traits.
Anitron Design. Choose one of the following options. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast using this trait (choose when you select the option).

Battle. You have proficiency in the Athletics or Intimidation skill, and you know the Deflection* cantrip. When you cast the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn’t require Concentration and its duration becomes 1 minute. You can’t modify it in this way again until you finish a Long Rest.
Diplomacy. You have proficiency in the Deception, Insight, or Persuasion skill, and you always have the Comprehend Languages spell prepared. You can cast it without a spell slot once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can also cast it using spell slots you have.
Technical. You have proficiency in the Computers, Medicine, or Technology skill, and with one tool of your choice. You also know the Mending cantrip, and its casting time is an action for you.

Integrated Tech. You have a built-in compartment that conceals a weapon, a tool, a Shield, or a piece of outrunning gear of your choice. If the chosen item has a proficiency associated with it, you gain that proficiency. The chosen item must weight 8 lb. or less, and a weapon must have the Light property. The item remains hidden until you deploy it as a Bonus Action (DC 20 to detect while stowed). You must have a free hand, and you hold the item or don the Shield as part of the Bonus Action. You stow the item (doffing a Shield) back in its compartment using another Bonus Action.
Recharge. You don’t need sleep, and magic can’t put you to sleep. During a Long Rest, you appear inert but remain conscious. You can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you consume a full Power Cell or connect to an energy source.
Robotic Resilience. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Petrified condition or the Poisoned condition.
Technological Being. You don’t gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, malnutrition, or suffocation.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/benthos.title: Benthos
neon-odyssey/species/benthos.content:
Benthos (BEN-thoess) are a people forever changed by the eldritch power of the Abyssal Void. Eons ago, their homeworld was ripped into a black hole and lost to the Wyrmways, the border dimension between the galaxy and the Void. They irrevocably transformed to survive the alien environment, taking on traits of the Void creatures known as the Deep. In time, they learned to harness dark matter, shaping it to their will and utilizing it in their magic and technology.
Benthos are diminutive people with features reminiscent of deep sea fish and skin in shades of the Void. They typically lack color outside their glowing circular eyes and lamp-like lures at the end of the flexible stalk that grows from their head. Their mouths are especially wide and can unhinge indefinitely.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Small (about 3-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Val’Shai
As a Benthos, you have these special traits.
Born of the Deep. You have Resistance to Necrotic and Psychic damage.
Dark Matter Crafting. While not in Bright Light, you can take a Magic action to shape shadows into one Small or smaller nonmagical item of your choice worth no more than $1,000. The item must appear in your hand, or in your space on a surface that can support it. The item disappears after a number of hours equal to your Proficiency Bonus or when it is reduced to 0 Hit Points. A creature that examines the object can discern its true nature with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check. The DC is 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and the ability modifier you chose for Lure of the Deep. Once you create an item with this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.
Lure of the Deep. You know the Dimness* cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have the Dissonant Whispers spell prepared, and starting at character level 5, you always have the Web spell prepared (the webs are spun shadow). You can cast each spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast the spells in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. You can make a target that fails its saving throw against your Dissonant Whispers move toward you instead of away. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the species).
One with Shadows. You can take the Hide action while only Lightly Obscured, even if you are within an enemy’s line of sight.
Swarming Shoal. When you deal damage while two or more of your allies are within 10 feet of you, you can deal an extra 1d4 Force damage to one target. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn. The damage die changes when you reach character levels 5 (1d6), 11 (1d8), and 17 (1d10).
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/bitling.title: Bitling
neon-odyssey/species/bitling.content:
Bitlings (BIT-ling) are a widely varied species that hail from the video game realm of Arcadia. The imaginative creativity and bombastic energy of the arcade plane infuse them with whimsical powers that change based on their inherent archetype—strong, swift, or soaring.
Bitlings often travel through Arcadia and the galaxy beyond seeking shiny collectibles that power their magic. Many set out on grand quests seeking fun adventures, sidekicks to befriend, and loot to add to their collection.
Unified by bright colors and exaggerated proportions, a bitlings’s appearance is only limited by one’s imagination. Their most common form is a bipedal animal of any variety, but there are those who resemble toy-like humanoids, walking inanimate objects, or even bizarre oblong shapes.
Creature Type: Fey
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Common on: Polygonia
As a Bitling, you have these special traits.
Collectible Drop. When you finish a Long Rest, you gain a token that looks like a digital collectible (coin, ring, gem, etc.). When you fail a D20 Test, you can expend one token to add 1d4 to the total, potentially causing it to succeed instead. When an enemy within 30 feet of you is reduced to 0 Hit Points, a token appears in its space and remains for 1 minute or until you collect it. You can have a maximum number of tokens equal to your Proficiency Bonus at one time.
Arcade Archetype. Your Arcadian nature grants you certain benefits. Choose

Soaring. ,
Strong. , or
Swift. : Soaring. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed while you’re not wearing Medium or Heavy armor. As a Magic action, you can expend a token and touch an ally to give it a Fly Speed equal to your Fly Speed for 1 minute. Strong. You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Additionally, once per turn when you hit a target with an attack roll, you can expend a token to push the target up to 20 feet straight away. If the target is an object, it takes double damage from your attack. Swift. Your Speed increases by 5 feet. As a Bonus Action, you can expend a token to take the Dash action. When you do, until the start of your next turn, your Speed is doubled and your movement doesn’t provoke Opportunity Attacks.

Checkpoint. As a Magic action, you can expend a token to create a shimmering checkpoint on a surface you touch. The checkpoint lasts for 24 hours or until you use this action again. While you’re on the same plane of existence, as a Magic action, you can teleport to the point, appearing in its space or the closest unoccupied space. When you do, you can expend a token to bring a willing creature you touch with you.
Respawn. When you drop to 0 Hit Points and don’t die outright, you can expend a token you’re carrying to drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/clawderan.title: Clawderan
neon-odyssey/species/clawderan.content:
Clawderan (klaw-DAIR-in) are an energetic species of humanoids with feline traits and are known to take pride in proving themselves in combat and other physical pursuits. Many seek glory to honor Myrmona the Paragon, the war goddess with whom they hold a cosmic connection.
While many clawderan seek the galactic battlefronts across the Stardust Rhapsody, some prefer to show off their athletic prowess through sports, dance, high-intensity industrial careers, and other such pursuits.
Clawderan builds range from agile to brawny and come in a variety of body and fur types, their feline traits resembling the full spectrum of cats both great and small. They typically have a short layer of fur across their bodies, with the notable exceptions being their manes, tails, and fluffy tufts that might grow on their torso or limbs.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 35 feet
Homeworld: Goro
As a Clawderan, you have these special traits.
Battle Ready. Once on your turn when you hit with an Unarmed Strike or an attack roll using a weapon with which you have proficiency, you can activate the Push, Slow, or Vex mastery property, in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that attack.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Eager Advance. When you roll Initiative, you can move up to your Speed.
Paragon’s Blessing. When you make an attack roll and roll an 18 or 19 on the d20, you can choose to make it a Critical Hit. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Limber Musculature. You have proficiency in the Acrobatics or Athletics skill, and you have Advantage on D20 Tests to avoid or end the Grappled or Restrained condition.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/cygnian.title: Cygnian
neon-odyssey/species/cygnian.content:
Cygnians (SIG-nee-in) are the star-touched of Agathos, once mortal beings remade by the will of the gods. Some were heroes who lived by the tenets of their favored deity so completely that they were chosen to ascend and begin their journey anew as a Celestial. Others were selected at birth due to prophecies of greatness in the stars, discovered places or relics of divine import, or caught the eye of a god on a whim.
While some live their new immortal lives in the heavenly realm of Agathos, many return to the galaxy to serve the god that reforged them
The physical form of cygnians is comprised of starstuff, with resilient skin and flowy hair that evoke the night sky and statues of sacred stone and metal. They typically share a humanoid visage adorned by star shapes with distinct features that reflect their god, but some retain traits of their original species.
Creature Type: Celestial
Size: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
As a Cygnian, you have these special traits.
Ageless. You don’t suffer from or die of old age.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Epic Resolve. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition.
Glory of Agathos. You are marked by one of the triads of Agathos:

Beacon. ,
Chronicle. ,
Fountain. , or
Tower. (choose the triad when you select this species). You can take a Bonus Action to gain a benefit determined by your triad. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend Heroic Inspiration to use it again. Beacon. For 1 minute, when you miss with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to reroll the d20 and use the new roll. Chronicle. Choose an ability score. For 1 minute, you can add a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus to saving throws using the chosen score. Fountain. Touch a creature and roll a number of d6s equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The target gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the total rolled, which vanish after 1 minute. Tower. For 1 minute, when you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage taken by 1d12 plus your Proficiency Bonus.

Made of Stars. You have Resistance to Radiant damage. When you take Radiant damage, you can take a Reaction to redirect some of the energy. The next time you deal damage before the end of your next turn, one target takes an extra 1d6 Radiant damage.
Starfall. When you fall at least 10 feet, you can take a Reaction to either slow or speed your fall until the start of your next turn. If you slow your fall, you fall only 60 feet and take no falling damage if you land during that time. If you speed your fall, you descend with comet-like force. You have Resistance to the fall’s damage, and one creature within 5 feet of you during the fall takes 2d6 Radiant damage.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/dathu.title: Dathu
neon-odyssey/species/dathu.content:
Dathu (DAH-thoo) are a ferocious people who have been transformed by the discordant tone of Instinct through their wrath and desire to tear down the perceived source of their pain. Despite this corruption, they remain free and can choose to restrain their aggressive urges or focus their rage on something rather than their impulse to commit mindless acts of destruction.
Many dathu follow pursuits that allow them to give in to their destructive nature, favoring groups and organizations they can link to their personal hivemind. Others surrender to their corruption and join the endless skittering swarms of cacophony.
Dathu possess insectile traits found in the forces of Instinct, with scaly skin and chitinous carapaces, often streaked with amber-colored resin. Their jaws are split into mandibles lined with jagged teeth that drip with corrosive acid.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Common on: Cicero Prime
As a Dathu, you have these special traits.
Ageless. You don’t suffer from or die of old age.
Acid Spray. You know the Acid Splash cantrip. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for it. You can modify the spell to cast it as a Bonus Action. When you cast the spell in this way, you can change the area to a 30-foot Line that is 5 feet wide that sprays from you. You can modify this spell a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Corrosive Blood. You have Resistance to Acid damage.
Hive Mind. You have telepathy with a range in feet equal to 10 times your character level.
Wrathful Devour. As an action, you can consume 1 pound of organic matter and expend and roll a Hit Point Die. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point).
Path of Instinct. When you reach character level 3, you must choose the path your discordant nature takes.

Swarm Survival. When you finish a Long Rest, you can choose a number of creatures you can see equal to your Proficiency Bonus and form a telepathic hive mind with them that lasts until you next finish a Long Rest. You and the chosen creatures can communicate telepathically with each other out to the range of your Hive Mind. Additionally, when you regain Hit Points from your Wrathful Devour trait, you can grant those Hit Points to one of the chosen creatures instead if they are within range of your Hive Mind.
Unending Hunger. Your creature type becomes Fiend. When you deal Acid damage to a creature, before the end of your next turn, you can use your Wrathful Devour trait as a Bonus Action (no additional organic matter required).

Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/flambego.title: Flambego
neon-odyssey/species/flambego.content:
Flambego (flahm-BAY-goh) are a colorful avian species that hail from idyllic tropical islands where life is leisurely. Bearing a mystical bond with the revelry god Xavrius the Celebrant, they are an easygoing people who prioritize relaxation and fun as major virtues.
Empowered by the magic of the party, most flambego seek to spread the carefree joy within them to people across the galaxy. They are often drawn to vacation destinations, but they won’t shy away from danger, especially when it threatens their chill vibes.
Flambego possess the traits of all manner of tropical birds, sporting vibrant, colorful plumage and wings that line each of their arms. Their proportions can vary, and while many have long legs, necks, and beaks, others are compact and round.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Prismara
As a Flambego, you have these special traits.
Celebrant’s Revelry. You know the Befriend* cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3 you always have the Heroism spell prepared, and when you reach character level 5, you always have the Lesser Restoration spell prepared. You can cast each spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose when you select this species).
Chill Under Pressure. You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed or Frightened condition.
Tropical Skies. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. If you’re wearing Medium or Heavy armor, or holding anything in your hands, you can’t use this Fly Speed.
Festive Flourish. Your jubilant nature manifests in flamboyant ways. When you finish a Long Rest, choose one of the following manifestations, which lasts until you finish your next Long Rest:

Good Vibes. Choose an ability score. You and your allies within 10 feet of you gain a bonus to saving throws that use that ability. The bonus is equal to the ability modifier you chose for Celebrant’s Revelry.
Relaxing Revel. You can lead up to eight creatures in lively song, dance, or other revelry for 1 minute. At the end of the revel, each creature gains the benefit of a Short Rest, regains one expended Hit Point Die, and its Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1. A creature can’t benefit from this manifestation again until it finishes a Long Rest.
Carefree Flight. Your Fly Speed becomes magical, and it no longer requires you to use your Arm Wings with free hands, and you can hover.

Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/glowblin.title: Glowblin
neon-odyssey/species/glowblin.content:
Glowblins (GLOH-blin) are small folk who feel big and intense emotions with an inner neon radiance. This emotionial glow colors their physical appearance and shines with vibrant light.
Many glowblins tap into this magic to entertain and influence, shaping light and sound to evoke powerful feelings. They’re drawn to fun, color, music, and all things maximalist.
Glowblins have colorful skin, hair, and luminous eyes that change to match their affinity for emotion and selfexpression, taking on a wide spectrum of hues and shades. They also have large, expressive ears, sharp teeth, and prominent, often pointed noses.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Small (about 3-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Prismara
As a Glowblin, you have these special traits.
Dazzle. You know the Dancing Lights cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have Color Spray prepared, and starting at character level 5, you always have Calm Emotions prepared. You can cast each spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells (choose the ability when you select this species).
Emotional Spectrum. Choose one of the options below; when you finish a Long Rest, you can choose a new option. Your chosen option can change your skin, hair, or eye color. As a Bonus Action, for the next minute, you shed Bright Light in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. You infuse the light with your chosen color and emotion to provide its benefit, and you can change your chosen color as part of the Bonus Action. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Blue or Teal. You and your allies within the light have Resistance to Psychic damage and have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Charmed or Frightened condition.
Green. When you or your allies in the light regain Hit Points, add your Proficiency Bonus to the number regained.
Orange. Your Speed increases by 10 feet. When an ally enters the light for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, its Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
Pink or Purple. Ability checks made to use the Influence action on an Indifferent creature in the light have Advantage.
Yellow. Double the range of your shed light. You and your allies in the light have Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Perception) checks. The first time an affected creature misses with an attack roll during this use of the light, the creature can add 1d4 to the total, possibly turning the miss into a hit.

Passionate Presence. You have proficiency in the Deception, Performance, or Persuasion skill.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/gorgonite.title: Gorgonite
neon-odyssey/species/gorgonite.content:
Gorgonites (GOR-guh-nite) are a species of serpentinefeatured humanoids that emerged from toxic jungles of beautiful but highly venomous flora and fauna. This has made them highly adapted to surviving poisonous environments and all of the threats within, in no small part to their powerful magical gaze.
Many of them have a deep appreciation for the balance of beauty and danger, accepting them as equal and necessary halves to a life truly lived. This can lead them to seek out death-defying opportunities across the galaxy.
Gorgonites have a skin of soft scales that range from earthy to vivid, with all manner of patterning. Instead of hair, gorgonites possess tendrils atop their head that resemble snake tails, which can be shaped into a variety of styles.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-6 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Sethreen
As a Gorgonite, you have these special traits.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Gorgon’s Gaze. As a Bonus Action, you can fix your gaze on a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The target is subjected to the effects of one of the options below (choose when you use the trait). The save DC is 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (choose the ability when you select this species). You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Beam. Eroding rays fire from your eyes. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 1d6 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This damage increases by 1d6 when you reach character levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6).
Hypnotic. Your eyes become captivating pools. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed condition for 1 minute. If you or your allies damage the target or force it to make a saving throw, the condition ends on it, and it is immune to your gaze for 24 hours.
Petrifying. Your eyes flare with dull color. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the Restrained condition for 1 minute as it partially turns to stone. A creature with Immunity to the Petrified condition succeeds automatically. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Keen Senses. You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.
Toxin Resistant. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/greeble.title: Greeble
neon-odyssey/species/greeble.content:
Greebles (GREE-bull) are a worm-like species driven by an innate desire to voyage across the galaxy. Said to be blessed by Pelogos the Navigator, they possess a supernatural ability to always sense the stars and navigate by their light.
Many greebles are drawn to space travel of all varieties, whether as transport pilots, explorers, or anything in between. This extrasensory power and internal cosmic compass is so strong that none can doubt the navigation skills of the greeble.
Despite their segmented worm biology, Greebles have a humanoid shape with nearly universally thin legs. They have pointed noses, disproportionately large eyes, and soft skin in shades of pink to more earthy tones.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (4-6 feet tall) or Small (3-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Sleema
As a Greeble, you have these special traits.
Cosmic Compass. You have proficiency with Navigation Tools and in the Survival skill.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Navigator’s Heading. You always have the Augury spell prepared, and you can cast it once without a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Whenever you cast the spell, if you can see the stars, you require no Material components. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose the ability when you select this species).
Segmented Biology. You have redundant internal organs. When an attack roll against you is a Critical Hit, you can take a Reaction to make it a normal hit instead. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Squirm. You have a Burrow Speed equal to your Speed. Additionally, you have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws to avoid or end the Grappled or Restrained conditions. When you fail such a roll, you can take a Reaction to expend and roll a Hit Point Die and add it to the total, possibly turning the failure into a success.
Stellar Navigator. You can see or sense the stars from anywhere in the galaxy, though they are faint during daylight or while an opaque object is between you and the sky. When you succeed on an ability check using Navigator’s Tools or the Survival skill while lost, or to avoid becoming lost, you gain Heroic Inspiration. You can’t gain Heroic Inspiration with this trait again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/isotron.title: Isotron
neon-odyssey/species/isotron.content:
Isotrons (EYE-soh-tron) are wholly digital beings brought to life by a synthetic soul called a hyperspark. Originating from the digital realm of the Hypergrid, they are comprised of code that can be compiled into physical forms of hard light. This grants them an innate ability to interface with computers and manipulate software with a touch.
Many isotrons live their entire lives within the Hypergrid, but others venture into physical reality to discover new experiences across the Stardust Rhapsody. In such a technological galaxy, isotrons have no trouble finding ways to put their inherent skills to use.
Isotron bodies vary in shape, size, and color, and they are often bedecked with bold or saturated hues that glow from the code within them. Their heads are typically humanoid with built-in visors, but some are entirely flat with a digital face projected upon it.
Creature Type: Construct
Size: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Common on: Megadyne
As an Isotron, you have these special traits.
Data Jump. You always have the Misty Step spell prepared. You can cast it without a spell slot a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. When you cast the spell using this trait while you are within 5 feet of a power or data connection, if your destination space is also within 5 feet of that connection, you don’t expend a use of this trait. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose the ability when you select this species).
Hard Light Body. You don’t gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, malnutrition, or suffocation.
Hypergrid Soul. You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.
Native Interfacing. You have proficiency in the Computers skill, and you can interface with a data port as if you were using a Spiking Deck by touching the port.
Surge Protection. You have Resistance to Lightning damage.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/jenovan.title: Jenovan
neon-odyssey/species/jenovan.content:
Jenovans ( jeh-NOH-vin) are the descendants of an artificial psionic species created through genetic experimentation to achieve a perfected lifeform. For eons, these bio-engineered creations intermingled with their creators until nothing but the jenovans remained, beings of enhanced physicality and fearsome telekinetic power.
Whatever homeworld they once had was lost to legend, so jenovans became a nomadic people who wander across the galaxy and settle numerous planets in tight-knit communities. They often strive to perfect themselves within and without, pushing their abilities to the limit and beyond. Many seek mightier challenges and opponents to test their skills and train against.
Jenovans have an appearance that betrays their genetically engineered origin, with unnaturally smooth skin in tones of gray, green, and purple. Their bodies are adorned with plates of natural armor as well as crystalline protrusions that focus their telekinesis. All jenovans bear either a prominent tail or a head tendril, though many have both.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
As a Jenovan, you have these special traits.
Bioengineered. You have proficiency in the Acrobatics, Athletics, or Stealth skill.
Psionic Deflection. When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to add your Proficiency bonus to your AC, possibly causing it to miss. If you make an attack miss this way, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you that isn’t behind Total Cover. The target takes 1d10 Force damage. You can take this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Telekinetic. You know the Kinetic Propulsion* cantrip and the Mage Hand cantrip (the hand is invisible). Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose the ability when you select this species).
Final Form. Starting at character level 3, you can transform as a Bonus Action and gain the benefits below. The transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you end it (no action required). Once you transform, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Energy Reversal. You can use your Psionic Deflection trait on attacks regardless of damage type.
Genetic Perfection. You gain Expertise in one of your skill proficiencies.
Kinetic Levitation. While you aren’t wearing Medium or Heavy armor, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.

Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/jozza.title: Jozza
neon-odyssey/species/jozza.content:
Jozza (JAW-zuh) are a hulking species of humanoids with shark-like features, hailing from a world covered almost entirely by oceans. They have a particular taste for blood and a biological penchant for violence, known best for their large jaws filled with razor-sharp teeth.
Many of them dive into fights with a rowdy glee, and their tough physicality makes them well suited to survive and push through any pain. However, some jozza prefer non-violent battles of wit and word or get their fix through virtual gameplay.
Jozza have coarse, gritty skin that can take on a wide range of colors, although many are shades of gray, blue, brown, and olive. A prominent dorsal fin rises from the top of their head or the back of their neck, and smaller fins grow on each of their arms. They sometimes have serrated exterior plates over their lower jaw or protruding bones at the hinges.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Kharabis
As a Jozza, you have these special traits.
Aquatic. You can breathe air and water, and you have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
Bloodhunt. You have Advantage on Wisdom checks to detect or track creatures that are missing any Hit Points.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Frenzied Fury. You have Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that is Bloodied.
Ignore Pain. When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to expend and roll one Hit Point Die. Reduce the triggering damage by an amount equal to the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier.
Violent Delight. When you deal damage while there is more than one enemy within 10 feet of you, you can deal an extra 1d4 damage. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn. The extra damage die increases in size when you reach levels 5 (1d6), 11 (1d8), and 17 (1d10).
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/laika.title: Laika
neon-odyssey/species/laika.content:
Laika (LIE-kuh) are a canine species that resemble bipedal dogs of any breed, with an innate sense of loyalty to their community and anyone they consider a packmate.
While all laika have a powerful bark and bite, most prefer to focus their efforts on cooperation and teamwork, particularly in the areas best suited to the talents of their respective canine lineage. Many of them strive to make a difference in their society, and a good number of historical laika have greatly benefited societies across the galaxy.
Laika come in all shapes, sizes, and physical characteristics that evoke canine breeds. They are covered in fur of varying length and thickness, which typically features naturalistic colors and patterns but can sometimes be vibrant and prismatic in hue.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Astrovega
As a Laika, you have these special traits.
Bite. You have sharp teeth you can use to make Unarmed Strikes with the Finesse property. When you deal damage with your bite, you can deal 1d8 Piercing damage plus your Strength modifier, instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike. You can grapple with your bite.
Keen Senses. You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.
Laika Lineage. You are part of a lineage that determines some of your traits. Choose a lineage from the Laika Lineages table. You gain the Trait benefit of that lineage immediately, and at character level 3, you gain the Pack Minded benefit.

You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Starting at character level 3, you and the target gain an additional benefit determined by your Laika Lineage.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/marsoom.title: Marsoom
neon-odyssey/species/marsoom.content:
Marsoom (mar-SOOM) are a bovine species with especially alien biology that grants them psionic prescience and highly tuned danger sense. They have adapted to the strange red planet they call home, making their physical prowess no less formidable.
Most marsoom believe that strength and safety come through unity, and they are typically welcoming to people of all creeds and origins. While they normally engage in diplomatic pursuits, marsoom are prepared to fight to defend what they value most.
They appear as sturdy bipedal cattle but have large, dark, oblong eyes with a third on their forehead. A pair of antennae sprouts from between their horns, their tails are split into two bushy ends, and their skin, hair, and tufts of fur come in a wide variety of vivid, unnatural colors.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-8 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Mavros
As a Marsoom, you have these special traits.
Cratering Jump. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash your inner strength to jump up to your Speed to an unoccupied space. When you land, you can unleash a shockwave in a 10foot Emanation originating from you. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 Thunder damage and is pushed or pulled (your choice) up to 10 feet toward or away from you. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Danger Sense. Your antennae tingle when danger is imminent. You have proficiency in the Perception skill. In addition, you can’t be surprised.
Herd Instinct. Once during your turn, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal damage, if you or an ally you can see took damage from that creature since the start of your last turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 Force damage.
Mighty Horns. You have a pair of horns, which you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. When you hit with an Unarmed Strike using your horns and deal damage with them, you can deal 1d8 Piercing damage plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage for an Unarmed Strike.
Split-Second Warning. When you are hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to force the attacker to reroll the d20 and use the lower roll. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/motlien.title: Motlien
neon-odyssey/species/motlien.content:
Motliens (MOT-lee-in) are an absurd people twisted by the discordant tone of Thrill through their indulgence in sensory overload to drown out their pain. They relish in antics and folly that spark maximum excitement, pleasure, and pain, all of which fuel their cartoonish and reality-warping magic.
Driven to be thrill seekers at heart, many Motliens crave the most dangerous or bombastic environments they can find. Others turn to sharing their laughter, fighting their darker impulses lest they join the hellish circus of Thrill.
Motliens resemble fools, jesters, and clowns, with rubbery, colorful skin marked with strange psychedelic or motley patterns. Their heads sprout fleshy tendrils that resemble a cap and bells, and they often have honkable noses, razorsharp teeth, and long, slithery tongues.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Common on: Cabaret
As a Motlien, you have these special traits.
Ageless. You don’t suffer from or die of old age.
Motley Tricks. You know the Minor Illusion and Vicious Mockery cantrips. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have the Hideous Laughter spell prepared, and starting at character level 5, you always have the Suggestion spell prepared. You can cast each of these spells once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).
Toon Force. You can take a Reaction when you gain one of the following conditions to end it before it takes effect: Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, Prone, or Stunned. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Twisted Mind. You have Resistance to Psychic damage.
Path of Thrill. When you reach character level 3, you must choose the path your discordant nature takes.

Honkweave. Your creature type becomes Fiend. As a Bonus Action, you can take on a wickedly cartoonish form for 1 minute. Once during each of your turns during that time, you can expend movement to teleport an equal distance to an unoccupied space you can see. Once you transform using this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Laugh it Off. You can use your Toon Force trait on an ally you can see within 30 feet of yourself when it gains one of the listed conditions. Additionally, when you end a condition using that trait, a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and the ability modifier you chose for Motley Tricks) or gain the condition you ended.

Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/murexian.title: Murexian
neon-odyssey/species/murexian.content:
Murexians (mer-EX-ee-in) are an aquatic species of mollusklike humanoids that emerged from the dark depths of an ocean world. Legend holds that they were created by Karkosa, the enigmatic proto-god of change, who imbued them with the ability to rapidly evolve to best survive the treacherous deep.
Evolution is core to all murexians, and they develop additional adaptations throughout their life to best suit them for their home environment and the galaxy beyond. This allows them to be equally comfortable on land as they are in the water. Many murexians have no fear of the future, trusting that they will adapt to whatever comes.
Murexians have mollusk-shell heads with tentacled faces that resemble cephalopods such as cuttlefish, and their rubbery skin can rapidly change in color and pattern to aid in communication. As they evolve and gain new adaptations, they can take on the physical characteristics of crustaceans and other invertebrates of the sea.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-6 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Kharabis
As a Murexian, you have these special traits.
Amphibious. You can breathe air and water, and you have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
Cold Resistance. You have Resistance to Cold damage.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.
Evolutionary Adaptation. You have evolved a gift from Karkosa. Choose one of the following options.

Chromatic. You have proficiency in the Deception or Persuasion skill, and you learn the Message cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.
Electrosensory. You have proficiency in the Insight or Perception skill. You gain Blindsight with a range of 10 feet, or increase any existing Blindsight’s range by 10 feet.
Traversal. You have proficiency in the Athletics or Stealth skill, and you gain your choice of a Burrow Speed or a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

Touch of Karkosa. When you reach character level 3, you evolve a defensive physical trait of your choice from the options below. You can use the chosen trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Camouflage. As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn. The condition ends early if you make an attack roll, cast a spell, or force a creature to make a saving throw.
Carapace. When you’re hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to force the attacker to reroll the d20 and use the lower roll.
Spines. When a creature within 30 feet of yourself hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to deal 1d6 Piercing damage plus your Proficiency Bonus to the attacker, and the attacker has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/navili.title: Navili
neon-odyssey/species/navili.content:
Navili (nuh-VEE-lee) are an ethereal folk who first stepped out of Arcadia and found a home in the Stardust Rhapsody. Their time among the mortal species changed them, but they never lost touch with the mystic power of their enchanted origin.
All navili embody a primary ideal—valor, might, or clarity— tracing back to the virtues of the sages that first guided them from Arcadia. Drawn to opportunities for heroism and to embody their chosen ideal, navili regularly seek secrets and relics within ancient ruins or lost temples.
They are typically willowy and graceful with skin that ranges from muted tones of nature to the brilliant blues, pinks, and greens of Arcadia, often marked with intricate runic patterns. Navili have shimmering eyes, broad noses, and leaf-like ears with several delicate points. A pair of prismatic, polygonal wings drift behind their backs.
Creature Type: Fey
Size: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Polygonia
As a Navili, you have these special traits.
Inventory Management. You can store and retrieve items from a digital inventory. With a Utilize Action, you can digitize an item you are wearing or carrying and store it in your inventory, or retrieve a digitized item into your hand and return it to normal. Your inventory can hold a number of items equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Digitized items appear in your space when you die.
Look! Listen!. You have proficiency in the Insight, Investigation, or Perception skill.
Polygon Wings. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed while you aren’t wearing Medium or Heavy armor.
Virtue of the Sages. You gain some traits based on the ideal you embody. Choose a virtue from the Virtues of the Sages table. You gain the level 1 benefit of that ideal.
When you reach character levels 3 and 5, you learn a spell as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).





























VirtueLevel 1Level 3Level 5ClarityYou know the Message cantrip. Additionally, you have Advantage on Intelligence saving throws and you have proficiency in Perception.Detect MagicZone of TruthMightYou know the Thunder Blast* cantrip. While you have the Frightened condition, you can still move closer to the source of your fear.HeroismAid
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/nematoan.title: Nematoan
neon-odyssey/species/nematoan.content:
Nematoans (NEE-muh-TOE-in) are a four-armed amphibian species with a voracious appetite. Their unique stomachs allow them to magically ingest traits of the things that they eat, temporarily enhancing their own abilities.
This has led many nematoans to develop a focus on food and seek out new dishes to taste across the galaxy. Some become chefs or ship’s cooks, while others get into dangerous trades where exotic and even black market delicacies can be procured.
Hailing from a world covered in putrid swamps, nematoans have physical traits that lend themselves to comfortable bog living, including webbed hands and feet, eye stalks, long tongues, and slimy skin that is typically earthy in tone.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Sleema
As a Nematoan, you have these special traits.
Amphibious. You can breathe air and water.
Four-Armed. You have two slightly smaller secondary arms below your primary pair of arms. You can use a secondary arm to manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down a Tiny object, or wield a weapon with the Light property.
Gourmand of Variety. You can eat part of any dead creature made of organic material. After 1 minute of eating, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d6 plus your Proficiency Bonus, and you can expend a Hit Point Die to regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the die plus your Constitution modifier. You can’t benefit from eating matter taken from the same creature until you finish a Long Rest.
Magic in the Meal. Your stomach draws power from what you’ve eaten. When you use your Gourmand of Variety trait, provided the creature died no more than 1 hour before, you can also gain an additional benefit depending on the creature’s highest ability score (choose in case of a tie). The benefit lasts for 1 hour, and for the duration, you have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws using that ability. Once you gain a benefit, you can’t gain that benefit again until you finish a Long Rest.

Strength. When you make a damage roll, you can reroll one of the dice and use the new roll.
Dexterity. Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
Constitution. If you have no Temporary Hit Points at the start of your turn, you gain a number of them equal to your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus.
Intelligence. You have telepathy with a range of 30 feet times your Proficiency Bonus, and you can cast Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible). Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.
Wisdom. You gain Blindsight with a range of 10 feet.
Charisma. The attitude of Hostile creatures improves to Indifferent toward you.

Tongue Lash. As a Bonus Action, you can lash out with your sticky tongue at a surface or object with a range of 15 feet. If the target is a Tiny or Small object, you can grab it with your tongue and pull it to you. If the target is a Medium or larger object or surface, you can pull yourself to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/nilari.title: Nilari
neon-odyssey/species/nilari.content:
Nilari (nih-LAR-ee) are the people of the void wyrm, which has granted them various draconic features that make them well suited to resisting the horrors of the Abyssal Void. While they were once the same progenitor species as the solari eons ago, the people who would become nilari chose to escape the doom of their homeworld by slipping into the Wyrmways and fusing their biology with the native creatures within.
All nilari have the blood of the wyrm, with many of them embracing this draconic lineage to steel their body and mind against all that would seek to corrupt and destroy them. Some take this further and pursue might in all its forms to stand against the darkness of the void.
Nilari are typically broader and beefier than their solari relatives, with physical traits of the void wyrm that manifest in varying ways, including pointed, fin-like ears, fleshy tendrils that grow along the jawline, jagged horns, plate-like scales, and claw-like hands. Their skin tends to have muted shades of purple, blue, or grayscale.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Val’Shai
As a Nilari, you have these special traits.
Breath Weapon. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of void energy in either a 15-foot Cone or a 30-foot Line that is 5 feet wide (choose the shape each time). Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus), taking 1d10 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This damage increases by 1d10 when you reach character levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10). You can use this Breath Weapon a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.
Psychic Fortitude. You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
Void Acclimation. You have Resistance to Necrotic damage and Psychic damage.
Wyrmhole Slip. As a Bonus Action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Until the end of the turn, the area within 10 feet of your starting or destination space (your choice) is Difficult Terrain for your enemies. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/oculok.title: Oculok
neon-odyssey/species/oculok.content:
Oculoks (AHK-yoo-lahk) are a cyclopean species that hails from a vast underground civilization. They are highly adapted to subterranean life with enhanced monocular vision that can see through inorganic matter and a magnetic touch that can manipulate metal to their needs.
Seeking opportunities to put their metal-bending to use, many oculoks possess a keen interest in building, from structures to vehicles. Their societies typically favor cooperation and rigid structure, and most citizens find purpose in contributing to a collective of any scale.
Oculoks have sturdy bodies covered in scaly, earth-toned skin and protruding armored nodules. Their heads are broad with lateral ridges and a spiked crown, with the most prominent feature being a large, singular eye. Their tails act as a built-in defense mechanism, ending in either a club or spikes.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Morzebe
As an Oculok, you have these special traits.
Cyclopean Focus. You have proficiency in the Insight, Investigation, or Perception skill.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.
Metal Shaper. You know the Mending cantrip. If you target a metal object, you can change the casting time to a Bonus Action. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose the ability when you select this species). Additionally, as a Magic action, you can touch a metal object (or part of a larger metal object or structure) no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The target gains Resistance or Vulnerability to all damage (your choice) for 1 minute. Once you use this action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Stonebreaking Tail. You have your choice of a spike or club on your tail that you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. When you hit with your tail and deal damage with it, you deal 1d8 Bludgeoning or Piercing damage, as appropriate, plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage for an Unarmed Strike.
Tunnel Vision. As a Bonus Action, you can adjust your vision to see through inorganic matter for up to 1 minute while you maintain Concentration on the vision. For the duration, you can see through objects and structures made of stone, metal, plastics, or similar materials to a range of 30 feet beyond the obstruction. The area you view through an object is Lightly Obscured. Living or once-living material of any thickness blocks your sight. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/oozoid.title: Oozoid
neon-odyssey/species/oozoid.content:
Oozoids (OO-zoid) are a pliable species of living slime that congealed from the remnants of the first primordial ooze that lingered from the creation of the cosmos. Despite their malleability, they have a brain, eyes, and nervous system that form them into a bipedal shape within a translucent membrane.
While they hail from the deep seas of ooze on their homeworld, oozoids have since spread across the galaxy, and some choose to don special pressurized suits to more easily hold their form in any environment. Many favor selfexpression across various media, including art and the creation of oblong “blobjects.”
Bright and highly saturated colors of slime typically comprise the wide variety of shapes and sizes of oozoids. Some favor a singular color, while others are multi-toned with strong gradients. Many choose to morph their heads to evoke hair-like shapes.
Creature Type: Ooze
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Tibbulus
As an Oozoid, you have these special traits.
Acid Resistance. You have Resistance to Acid damage.
Amorphous. You have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and you can move through a space as narrow as 1 foot without expending extra movement to do so.
Elastic Lunge. You add 10 feet to your maximum Long Jump distance and 5 feet to your maximum High Jump distance. You have Resistance to damage you take from falling.
Malleable Reach. Your reach with Melee weapons, Unarmed Strikes, and your hands to manipulate objects increases by 5 feet. Additionally, when you hit with an Unarmed Strike and deal damage with it, you can deal Acid damage equal to 1d6 plus your Strength modifier, instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike.
Reconstitution. As a Magic action, you expend and roll one Hit Point Die. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier. Alternatively, when you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can immediately use this trait (no action required), and you can’t activate it this way again until you finish a Long Rest.
Tremorsense. You have Tremorsense with a range of 60 feet.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/pakku.title: Pakku
neon-odyssey/species/pakku.content:
Pakku (PAH-koo) are a species of sapient plants with the combined elements of cacti and carnivorous flora. To survive their deadly, venomous homeworld, they have developed a variety of adaptations to overcome both predators and prey.
Favoring the more lawless corners of the galaxy, pakku usually seek their fortune through grit and resolve. Many of them have a strong interest in the crafting and handling of weapons, especially firearms, striving to master the art of the duel with their implement of choice.
Widely varied in shape and size, pakku appear as bipedal plants with spiny cactus bodies that are usually a shade of green. Their heads are typically topped with hair-like vines or colorful, exotic flowers with extra-wide, toothy mouths that resemble carnivorous plants.
Creature Type: Plant
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Sethreen
As a Pakku, you have these special traits.
Cactus Spines. Your body is covered in fine, sharp spines you can use to make Unarmed Strikes or use as a Thrown weapon with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. When you hit with your spines and deal damage with them, you can deal 1d6 Piercing damage plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage for an Unarmed Strike. Your spines have the Finesse property.
Dissolving Enzymes. When you deal damage with an Unarmed Strike, a weapon with the Thrown property, or your Prickly Skin trait, you can deal an extra 1d6 Acid or Poison damage. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Fibrous Body. You have Resistance to Acid and Poison damage.
Photosynthesis. When you finish a Short Rest in Bright Light and expend Hit Point Dice to regain Hit Points, you can roll each expended die twice and use the higher roll. After using this trait, you don’t gain Exhaustion levels from malnutrition for 24 hours.
Prickly Skin. When a creature grapples you, it takes 1d6 Piercing damage.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/poggle.title: Poggle
neon-odyssey/species/poggle.content:
Poggles (PAW-gull) are born lucky. Said to be the creation of the luck goddess Tykris the Dealer, the favor of fortune touches everything they do. While they use this blessing to seek prosperous and happy lives, they also can share their innate luck with others.
Drawn to games of chance, they can be found at gambling tables across the galaxy. Some use their death-defying fortune to take extremely dangerous jobs where a little luck is required for survival. Others find themselves in the world of finance, amassing their wealth through risky investments.
Poggles are a diminutive species covered in fur that is typically white, brown, gray, or pink, though it can grow in other hues. They have long, sometimes-floppy ears, small, bat-like wings on their back, and a wire-like tail that ends in a colorful puff ball.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Small (about 2-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Prismara
As a Poggle, you have these special traits.
Dealer’s Favor. You have 4 Luck Dice which are d6s, and you regain 1d4 expended Luck Dice when you finish a Long Rest. When you or a creature you can see within 10 feet of you makes a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to expend and roll 1 Luck Die and apply it as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the total. The maximum number of Luck Dice you have increases at levels 5 (6 dice), 11 (8 dice), and 17 (10 dice). Additionally, the number of expended Luck Dice you regain increases when you reach levels 5 (1d6), 11 (1d8), and 17 (1d10).
Flutter Flight. Because of your wings, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. You can’t use this Fly Speed if you’re wearing Medium or Heavy armor.
Go-To Game. You have proficiency with one Game Set of your choice.
Lucky Knack. You have proficiency in one skill of your choice.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/raizo.title: Raizo
neon-odyssey/species/raizo.content:
Raizo (RYE-zoh) are a people born of the storm, and they all carry the power and ferocity of a raging tempest within them. Hailing from a world beset by never-ending, violent storms, they possess the supernatural ability to unleash the power of thunder, lightning, and rain to overcome staggering odds.
They typically have a fearlessness against danger and overwhelming obstacles, often conquering any barrier in their way. This relentlessness has allowed many to master the elements and thrive in harsh, inhospitable environments.
Raizo are typically tall, solidly built, and often heavily muscled. A pair of horns grow from the top of their foreheads, and they sport tusks from their lower jaw. Their skin runs in shades of red, blue, green, gray, or yellow. Many raizo display tattoos that reflect particularly important aspects of their nature or personality.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 6-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Goro
As a Raizo, you have these special traits.
Fury of the Tempest. You have proficiency in the Athletics, Intimidation, or Survival skill.
Storm Magic. You know the Shocking Grasp and Thunder Blast* cantrips, and Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them (choose when you select this species). You can cast the spells as a Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Tempest Resistance. You have Resistance to Lightning damage and Thunder damage.
Wrathful Resilience. If you fail a Strength or Constitution saving throw, you can expend a Hit Point Die to reroll the d20 and use the new roll.
Unleash the Storm. When you reach character level 3, you can release your inner storm as a Bonus Action, using one of the options below (choose each time you use this trait). The storm lasts for 1 minute or until you end it (no action required). Once you take this Bonus Action, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest. For the duration, you create a storm in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you, and once on each of your turns, when you deal damage with an attack or a spell, you can deal extra damage to one target of a type determined by the storm options. The extra damage equals your Proficiency Bonus. Here are the storm options:

Lightning Spirit (Lightning Damage. ). At the end of each of your turns, each creature of your choice in the Emanation takes Lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Tempest Born (Cold Damage. ). You and your allies in the Emanation have Half Cover from ranged attacks.
Thunder Soul (Thunder Damage. ). At the start of each of your turns, each creature of your choice in the Emanation must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and the ability modifier you chose for Storm Magic) or be pushed up to 10 feet away from you. A creature that fails the save by 5 or more has the Prone condition.

Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/rangor.title: Rangor
neon-odyssey/species/rangor.content:
Rangor (RAING-gor) are a hulking, subterranean species with an inherent supernatural force of momentum brought on by the aether that suffuses their core. They can propel themselves forward at surprising speeds given their bulk and have the innate ability to become an unstoppable force that can smash through anything in their way.
Having first burrowed out of an asteroid of crystalized aether, rangor typically have a wanderlust that keeps them in outer space. Many of them stay on the move and stop for limited periods of time at space stations, moons, asteroids, and other off-world locations.
Rangor generally have broad, bulky builds with proportionally long arms that end in digging claws and short legs. Their thick hides are mottled with patches of tough scales, and they grow flaps of skin that resemble shaggy hair. A rangor’s nostrils sit in the middle of their forehead, and their short tusks continue to grow as they age.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Titan IX
As a Rangor, you have these special traits.
Burrowing. You have a Burrow Speed equal to your Speed.
Claws. You have claws you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. When you hit and deal damage with them, you can deal 1d8 Slashing damage plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike, and the target also has the Grappled condition.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.
Momentum. You can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action. When you do so, the next time you deal damage before the end of the turn, the target takes extra Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Powerful Build. You have Advantage on D20 Tests you make to end the Grappled condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.
Unstoppable Force. Starting at character level 3, when you use your Momentum trait, you become an overwhelming focal point of force until the end of the turn. For the duration, the damage die of your claws increases to 1d10, you ignore Difficult Terrain, you deal double damage to objects and structures, and you can move into the space of an object and make one Unarmed Strike against it. If you destroy the object with that attack, you can keep moving, otherwise you return to the space you left and your movement ends.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook

neon-odyssey/species/saurian.title: Saurian
neon-odyssey/species/saurian.content:
Saurians (SOR-ee-in) are the oldest species in the Stardust Rhapsody, appearing as humanoid versions of the galaxy’s numerous dinosaurs and similarly prehistoric reptiles. They bear a special connection with the Harmony and can channel its lifegiving energies through that spark.
This connection manifests in an intimate ancestral connection that grants them special insight on how to approach their daily lives.
Across five distinct lineages, saurians comprise a wide range of body types and statures, with each one reminiscent of a broader category of dinosaur. These grant them the traits of water-dwellers, fliers, predators, scavengers, and hardy grazers. They typically have naturalistic hues, but some have vibrantly prismatic scales.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Krayta
As a Saurian, you have these special traits.
Ancestral Memory. You have proficiency in the Arcana, History, or Religion skill.
Harmonious Conduit. As a Magic action, you touch a creature and roll a number of d6s equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The target regains a number of Hit Points equal to the total rolled. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Natural Weapon. You have a natural weapon you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. It deals 1d6 damage of a type appropriate to the weapon instead of the normal damage; Bludgeoning for a slam (club, tail, or headbutt), Piercing for a bite or gore, or Slashing for a claw. Your
Saurian Lineage. You are part of a lineage that determines some of your physical characteristics and traits. Choose a lineage from the Saurian Lineages table and gain the benefits of that lineage.

In addition, you can hold your breath for a number of hours equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).QuickclawBite or ClawYou have proficiency in the Stealth skill, and while you are Lightly Obscured, you can hide while in an enemy’s line of sight.RockhideSlam or GoreYou have a +1 bonus to AC; your Hit Point maximum increases by 1, and by 1 again each time you gain a level.SharptoothBiteYou can make a bite attack as a Bonus Action. Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
