neon-odyssey/species/skettik.title: Skettik
neon-odyssey/species/skettik.content:
Skettiks (SKEH-tik) are a flightless avian species suffused with innate necromantic energy, the remnants of a cataclysmic ritual that killed and reanimated the world soul of their homeworld. These warped carrion-eaters use their necrotic magic to craft personal minions or strange relics from bone.
Many skettiks are reclusive, shying away from places touched by garish sunlight, and often find themselves operating in the galaxy’s criminal underworld. Others find great success in business and as merchants, utilizing their shrewdness and skepticism to score the best deals.
Skettiks resemble wingless vultures in a humanoid shape with scaly skin and sparse patches of feathers that range from grayscale to drab shades of other colors. They have long claws on their hands and feet that they use for climbing the huge trees of their homeworld, and their jagged beaks are filled with sharp teeth for cracking bone.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-6 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Vulx
As a Skettik, you have these special traits.
Bonecraft. With 1 minute of work, you can magically shape bone into useful forms. You can create a piece of outrunning gear that doesn’t require power and is worth $500 or less, or a Simple weapon that lacks the Ammunition or Powered properties, using an amount of bone equal to the weight of the item. The item crumbles to dust after 24 hours.
Carrion Eater. You can eat spoiled food without issue. Additionally, you have Resistance to Poison damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
Canopy Climber. You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.
Channeled Necrosis. When you deal damage, you can change the damage type to Necrotic.
Necromantic Curse. You know the Culling* cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have the Inflict Wounds spell prepared, and at character level 5, you always have the Construct Companion* (the Construct is made of bone) spell prepared. You can cast each spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose ability when you select this species).
Rotproof. You have Resistance to Necrotic damage.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/solari.title: Solari
neon-odyssey/species/solari.content:
Solari (soh-LAH-ree) are the people of the solar phoenix, which has imbued them with the essence of the sun and an inherent connection to the cycle of rebirth. While they were once the same progenitor species as the nilari eons ago, the people who would become solari chose to accept their fate when their homeworld’s sun exploded and turned the planet to ash. However, once they were consumed by the blazing radiance, they were reborn as an entirely new species by the will of Alara the Lightbringer.
They typically exhibit the unbound passion of the Lightbringer, pursuing that which they value and love with vivacious zeal. Many solari seek to share their inner light and passion with people across the galaxy, guiding them toward lofty achievement.
Solari tend to be gracefully built, with especially long, pointed ears and floating hair that spans a gradient of vibrant hues. Their soft skin can have the tone of any of the galaxy’s countless suns, ranging broadly from typical oranges, yellows, reds, and pinks to rarer blues, violets, and beyond.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-6 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Adonia
As a Solari, you have these special traits.
Enduring Passion. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to give the target Heroic Inspiration. The target can choose to use it on the triggering roll. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Illuminate. You know the Light cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose the ability when you select this species).
Lightbringer’s Glare. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash a blaze of solar radiance. Each creature of your choice within a 15-foot Emanation originating from you takes Radiant damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Phoenix Rising. Immediately after you succeed or fail on a Death Saving Throw, you can ignore the result and regain Hit Points equal to your level. You immediately rise to your feet and use Lightbringer’s Glare (no action required). You don’t expend a use of that trait, and the size of its Emanation increases to 30 feet for this use. Other creatures of your choice in that area regain Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Solar Mettle. You have Resistance to Radiant damage.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook

neon-odyssey/species/stardust-human.title: Stardust Human
neon-odyssey/species/stardust-human.content:
Humans are the most populous species of the Stardust Rhapsody by a wide margin, and they can be found on virtually every habitable planet across the galaxy. They have no singular homeworld, and legend says that they simply stepped out of the Harmony on all worlds simultaneously one day.
They are highly adaptable and can make a comfortable life no matter where they’re from or where they choose to settle down. In the face of trials, tribulations, and hardships, the indomitable human spirit oftentimes prevails, allowing them to overcome whatever challenges they face and complete whatever hero’s journey they are set on by fate.
Humans are as diverse in appearance as they are in personality, and come in all shapes, sizes, colors, and physical attributes.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall) chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
As a Stardust Human, you have these special traits.
Harmonic Control. As a Bonus Action, you can roll one Hit Point Die without expending it to regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Proficiency Bonus. You can use this trait once, and you regain the use of it when you finish a Long Rest.
Indomitable Spirit. When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed on it instead. Once you use this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
Overcome. When you roll a 1 or a 20 on a D20 Test, you gain Heroic Inspiration. If the roll has no stakes or consequences when you make it, this trait doesn’t function.
Planetary Adaptation. You gain an Origin feat of your choice that has a homeworld prerequisite.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/tekal.title: Tekal
neon-odyssey/species/tekal.content:
Tekal (teh-KAHL) are a people constructed from stone, crystal, and plant matter, powered by Harmonyte gemstone technology. Their souls are manifested from the vital and somber energies of the Harmony itself, granting them the ability to harness the cycle of life and death.
Many tekal have an unbound curiosity in the natural world and a sense of wonder in discovering all aspects of the Stardust Rhapsody and galactic living. Their affinity to the unique intersection of harmonic and primordial powers typically grants them a unique appreciation for all living things.
Tekal have solidly built bodies embedded with gemstones and glowing patterns of inlaid crystal that evoke the circuitry of their natural technology. They have typically humanoid faces and plants that grow from their heads to resemble hair.
Creature Type: Construct
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Krayta
As a Tekal, you have these special traits.
Crystalline Resilience. You have Resistance to Poison damage and Radiant damage. You also have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Petrified condition or the Poisoned condition.
Durable Construction. You don’t gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, malnutrition, or suffocation.
Grounded Recharge. If you are in contact with the bare ground of a planet with a world soul, you don’t need to sleep, and you can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a motionless, inactive state.
Harmony Flux. The essence of Harmony fills you. You know the Culling* and Druidcraft cantrips. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you can cast the following spells without a spell slot: Cure Wounds or Ray of Sickness. Once you cast one of these spells, you can’t cast either of them in this way again until you finish a Long Rest. Starting at character level 5, you can cast the following spells without a spell slot: Blindness/Deafness or Lesser Restoration. Once you cast one of these spells, you can’t cast either of them again in this way until you finish a Long Rest. You always have these spells prepared, and you can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose the ability when you select this species).
Nature Affinity. You can communicate in a limited manner with Beasts, Monstrosities, Plants, and vegetation. They understand the meaning of your words, though you can’t understand them in return. You have Advantage on ability checks made to sway them using the Influence action.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/terminox.title: Terminox
neon-odyssey/species/terminox.content:
Terminox (TER-mi-noks) are a bio-mechanical people reforged by the discordant tone of Progress through the hyper-logical denial of emotion to build structures of control around their pain. Their indomitable bodies are designed to neither cease nor slow in the face of whatever obstacle stands before them.
Typically driven to achieve perfection in the areas of their obsession, terminox are always seeking the next step of optimization. While some uphold an advancement of the self, finding a solitary path or embedding in a small unit, many assimilate into the collective and join the never-ending march of Progress.
Terminox are a species built of fiendish metal with cables of synthetic flesh that cling to their frame like muscle. Their heads appear approximately skeletal, sometimes connected to cords that resemble hair. The parts that make up their construction are typically colored in shades of gray or red.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Common on: Megadyne
As a Terminox, you have these special traits.
Ageless. You don’t suffer from or die of old age.
Conductive Frame. You have Resistance to Lightning damage.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Relentless March. When you drop to 0 Hit Points but aren’t killed outright, you can choose to ignore the effects of the Unconscious condition until you regain any Hit Points. You must still make Death Saving Throws until you regain any Hit Points or become Stable. If you take an action while you are at 0 Hit Points, you suffer a Death Saving Throw failure unless that action stabilizes you or restores you to 1 Hit Point or more. Once you ignore the Unconscious condition with this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
Strength of Metal. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Petrified and Poisoned conditions.
Path of Progress. When you reach character level 3, you must choose the path your discordant nature takes.

Adaptive Plating. Your creature type becomes Fiend. When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to change the damage type of your Conductive Frame trait to the triggering damage type for 1 minute. You can end the change early at any time (no action required). You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Collective Protocol. While you can see at least one ally within 60 feet of yourself, when you or one such ally fails a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to grant a bonus to the total equal to your Proficiency Bonus, possibly turning the failure into a success. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/varg.title: Varg
neon-odyssey/species/varg.content:
Vargs (VAHRG) are a vampiric people corrupted by the discordant tone of Entropy through the envious yearning to fill the emptiness within them in the hopes it may quiet their pain. They hunger for the life essence of others, which they drain to briefly satiate themselves. Those who work to control or even master this craving avoid succumbing to its addictive nature. The rest become ravenous killers.
Whether enticed by the ease of feeding within heavily populated areas or brooding in the remote reaches of far-flung worlds, the desire of a varg to fill the pit within themselves often leads them to achieve impressive levels of wealth or power—though it is never enough.
Vargs have pallid skin in desaturated hues, and on their backs are leathery flaps that resemble cloaks. They typically have prominent foreheads, ears that evoke bat wings, and prominent fangs. All vargs have one or more patches of fiendish energy on their chest, neck, or abdomen that serve as windows to the emptiness within.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 2-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Common on: Noxilus
As a Varg, you have these special traits.
Ageless. You don’t suffer from or die of old age.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Drain Energy. You know the Chill Touch cantrip, and Constitution is your spellcasting ability for it. You can cast the spell as a Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Hollow Flesh. You have Resistance to Cold damage and Necrotic damage.
The Pit Within. You don’t gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration or malnutrition, but you must drain vital energy to survive. If you go a number of days equal to your Constitution modifier plus 1 (minimum of 1) without damaging a creature with your Chill Touch, you gain 1 Exhaustion level. Until you damage a creature with Chill Touch, you can’t remove Exhaustion levels, and you continue to gain 1 Exhaustion level every 24 hours that pass. This trait can’t cause your Exhaustion level to rise higher than 5. If you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points using Chill Touch, you remove all Exhaustion levels gained from this trait.
Path of Entropy. When you reach character level 3, you must choose the path your discordant nature takes.

Distant Desire. Your Chill Touch cantrip now has a range of 60 feet. When you damage a creature with it, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Wings of Night. Your creature type becomes Fiend, and you grow a pair of bat wings from your shoulders that grant you a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. When you cast Chill Touch, you can wrap your wings around the target to gain Advantage on the spell’s attack roll.

Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/volcar.title: Volcar
neon-odyssey/species/volcar.content:
Volcar (VOAL-car) are a species of earth and fire, with fully elemental bodies of lava that they can melt and solidify at will. Able to sustain themselves entirely on minerals, they are a hearty people who thrive on their volcanic homeworld.
Many volcar are fascinated by and study cycles, especially the relationship between destruction and renewal. They are often nomadic, following seasons, currents, patterns, and other natural phases. Some prefer more social or political cycles, getting involved in governments or militaries.
Their rocky hide runs a variety of earthen shades from dark obsidian to pale limestone, with a humanoid visage that appears like a chiseled statue or a natural rock formation. Glowing lava forms lines and patterns in their exterior and can ignite at a moment’s notice, turning their whole form redhot and malleable.
Creature Type: Elemental
Size: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Caldoa
As a Volcar, you have these special traits.
Furnace Metabolism. You don’t gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, and you can eat minerals and glass as if they were a similar amount of food.
Hot Lava. You know the Produce Flame cantrip. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for it.
Igneous Hide. You have Resistance to Fire damage and Poison damage. You also have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Petrified condition or the Poisoned condition.
Molten Form. As a Bonus Action, you can melt your rocky body into lava for 1 minute, until you have the Incapacitated condition, or until you end it early (no action required). For the duration, you have Immunity to Fire damage, you can move through spaces as narrow as 1 foot without spending extra movement to do so, and you can move through a creature’s space as if it were Difficult Terrain. When you move through a creature’s space, you can deal 1d4 Fire damage to it. A creature takes this damage only once per turn. The damage increases by 1d4 when you reach character levels 5 (2d4), 11 (3d4), and 17 (4d4). Your equipment shapes with your molten form and is unharmed by this transformation. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Solidified Obsidian. When you are hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to add your Proficiency Bonus to your AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/yaungu.title: Yaungu
neon-odyssey/species/yaungu.content:
Yaungu (YAWN-goo) are a hearty people born of the cold, bearing a deep, supernatural connection to ice and snow. Having descended from the giants of the frozen mountains and tundras of their frigid homeworld, they have adapted to thrive and build remarkable civilizations in the most inhospitable of environments.
Many yaungu have a deep appreciation for the sharing of and passing down of knowledge, whether it be through story, song, or written text. Some even seek out well-hidden truths or heavily guarded secrets so that the learnings can be shared by the many to lead to a brighter future.
Yaungu tend to be tall and powerfully built, with long arms and prominent claws for climbing. Horns grow from the sides of their head, which many of them decorate with carvings or other adornments. Their shaggy, insulating fur is typically white or some shade of blue, but some yaungu sport pelts of brown, gray, or black.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Bortuun
As a Yaungu, you have these special traits.
Blizzard Cunning. You have Blindsight with a range of 5 feet. As a Bonus Action, you can increase the range to 20 feet for 10 minutes. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Frigid Resilience. You have Resistance to Cold damage.
Frozen Soul. As a Magic action, you create ice, freeze water, or shape existing ice that fills up to a 5-foot Cube. You can decide the shape the ice takes, though the forms are simple or crude unless you have proficiency in appropriate tools to create intricate or complex shapes. Unless the environment is freezing cold, the ice lasts for 1 minute and then melts or vanishes. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Long Arms. You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and your reach with your arms increases by 5 feet.
Powerful Build. You have Advantage on any D20 Test you make to end the Grappled condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.
Torpid Chill. When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage, you can deal an extra 1d6 Cold damage. Unless the target has Resistance or Immunity to Cold damage, it also has Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws until the end of your next turn. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/yoggoth.title: Yoggoth
neon-odyssey/species/yoggoth.content:
Yoggoths (YAW-goth) are a strange species rumored to have been birthed from the eldritch dreams of the mysterious elder beings of the galaxy. Hailing from a remote homeworld scattered with the ruins of their creators, they experience otherworldly dreams said to be an echo of what brought their people into being.
As the ultimate survivors, yoggoths are extremely resourceful and prone to recycling everything they possibly can. Many are drawn to salvaging operations, but some are driven to uncover the mysteries of their dreams and eldritch origins, not stopping until they discover the answers they seek.
Yoggoths appear like alien flies in a bipedal humanoid shape with both leathery and chitinous hides that are typically earthy in color. They have large glassy eyes, four nostrils on their elongated snouts, and fleshy tendrils that can grow from their head or chin. Two pairs of leathery wings grow from their shoulders, from which they emit their infamous drone.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: K’Thar
As a Yoggoth, you have these special traits.
Buzzing Wings. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. You can’t use this Fly Speed if you’re wearing Medium or Heavy armor.
Hypnagogic Droning. As a Bonus Action, you can create a vibration that resonates with your most alien dreams in a 20-foot Emanation originating from you. The droning lasts for 1 minute or until you lose your Concentration. When you create the Emanation, and at the start of each of your turns for the duration, each creature of your choice in that area must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or subtract 1d4 from ability checks and attack rolls until the start of your next turn. Once you use this Bonus Action, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Lingering Dreams. When you sleep, your dreams connect to the lingering echoes of the Eldest that created the yoggoth species, gifting you with knowledge you can’t explain. When you finish a Long Rest, you gain proficiency in one skill and with one tool of your choice until you make a different selection with this trait.
Sole Survivor. You have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Charmed, Exhaustion, or Poisoned conditions.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/zamani.title: Zamani
neon-odyssey/species/zamani.content:
Zamani (zuh-MAH-nee) are a people with an inherent, supernatural connection to time itself. They perceive time and their place in it differently than every other species of the galaxy, allowing them to look into the immediate future and see numerous outcomes. Between this and their physical adaptation to handle heat, zamani thrive on their harsh desert homeworld.
Many zamani have a stoic philosophy of acceptance, and many of the worries of day-to-day life can seem insignificant in the grand scheme of time. While some believe that their temporal powers make them the masters of their own fate, others believe nothing can be done to change one’s destiny.
Zamani have sun-tempered skin that runs from dark earth shades to muted jewel tones with embedded gemstones that focus their inherent energies. Their heads have raised ridges and plates that serve as heat sinks, and their bodies are typically covered in elaborate, geometric patterns of gold that evoke the flow of time.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-6 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Shensaati
As a Zamani, you have these special traits.
Desert Adaptation. You have Resistance to Fire Damage.
Reversion. When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to gain Resistance to that damage and teleport to an unoccupied space you can see that you occupied since the start of your previous turn. You can use this trait once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Temporal Control. You have Advantage on Initiative rolls. When you roll Initiative, you can treat a d20 result of 9 or lower as a 10.
Temporal Glimpse. When you finish a Long Rest, you look at fragments of possible futures. Roll a d20 and record the number. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself makes a D20 Test, you can replace the test with the recorded number. You must choose to do so before the roll. The glimpse can only be used once, and you lose an unused glimpse when you finish a Long Rest.
Timing is Everything. When you fail a D20 Test, you can add 1d4 to the total, possibly turning the failure into a success. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook
Species

neon-odyssey/species/zephursa.title: Zephursa
neon-odyssey/species/zephursa.content:
Zephursa (zeh-FUR-suh) are a small, ursine species that hail from floating cities atop a sea of clouds. They bear a special connection to the skies, allowing them to call the wind and even puff up in a cloudy form. They value the power of friendship, which they can genuinely manifest and harness to overcome challenges.
With a spark of ingenuity and a clever knack for invention, many Zephursa are drawn to tinkering with gizmos and developing new ways of approaching daily tasks. Many zephursa are most comfortable soaring through the skies of worlds across the galaxy, but there are those who stay more grounded and find their joy in the community that surrounds them.
Zephursa are little humanoid bears with colorful fur, often with pastel hues although more natural colors do appear. They have swirling cloud patterns somewhere on their coat that sometimes grow into bushier tufts of fluff. The clouds that encircle them when they puff up usually take on the prismatic color of their fur.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Small (about 3-4 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Tibbulus
As a Zephursa, you have these special traits.
Children of the Skies. You know the Befriend* cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have the Fog Cloud spell prepared, and starting at character level 5, you always have the Gust of Wind spell prepared. You can cast each one once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).
Cloud Puff. As a Bonus Action, you can puff up with swirling cloud stuff and gain a Fly Speed equal to half your Speed for 1 minute. When you are hit by an attack roll during this time, you can take a Reaction to subtract 1d4 from the total, possibly causing it to miss. Once you puff up with this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Gentle Descent. While you don’t have the Incapacitated condition, when you fall, your rate of descent is 60 feet per round, and you take no damage from falling.
Soothing Stare. As a Magic action, you target a creature you can see within 30 feet of you and end one of the following conditions affecting it: Charmed, Frightened, or Stunned. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/zeticulan.title: Zeticulan
neon-odyssey/species/zeticulan.content:
Zeticulans (zeh-TIK-yoo-lin) are one of the oldest and most enigmatic species of the Stardust Rhapsody, with some theorizing that they impossibly arrived from outside the galaxy. Their minds are so expansive that they have unlocked a psionic power that emanates past their own bodies and allows them to pierce into the minds of others using telepathy.
Many zeticulans crave k nowledge above all else, desiring to study, understand, and catalog every aspect of existence down to its last atom. They are drawn to any opportunity to conduct experiments of all varieties or the chance to expand their mental databases. While many remain elusive and mysterious, there are some who venture to mingle with other peoples of the galaxy to learn through new and unpredictable life experiences. njjjjh ]
Varying in size and shape, zeticulans are alien humanoids with smooth skin that is typically gray or green. They have thin, elongated necks, oversized, bulbous craniums, and large, dark eyes with slit-like pupils. Among the hairless majority, a few can grow shocks of vibrant, nearly neon hair atop their heads.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Mavros
As a Zeticulan, you have these special traits.
Alien Mind. You have Resistance to Psychic damage.
Big Brained. You have proficiency in the Insight, Investigation, or Persuasion skill.
Mental Speech. You have telepathy with a range of 10 feet times your character level.
Repulsion Field. As a Bonus Action, you can project a psychic field in a 15-foot Emanation originating from you that deters your enemies. Until the start of your next turn, you and your allies within the Emanation don’t provoke Opportunity Attacks when leaving an enemy’s reach. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Telepathic. You know the Psychic Needle* cantrip. Additionally, starting at character level 3, you always have the Command spell prepared, and starting at character level 5, you always have the Detect Thoughts spell prepared. You can cast each of these spells once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast using this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).
Source: Overdrive Expansion
Species

neon-odyssey/species/zorbrak.title: Zorbrak
neon-odyssey/species/zorbrak.content:
Zorbraks (ZOR-brak) are a bipedal insectile species that have mantis-like features and boast a secondary pair of powerful scythe-like appendages in addition to their arms. They are the consummate hunters with a powerful predator’s instinct and the supernatural ability to stalk their prey.
Zorbraks typically lack any sense of fear, allowing them to seek and kill the most dangerous game across the galaxy without hesitation. Many are instilled with immense pride by the hunting trophies they have won over their lifetime and are driven by the desire to leave a legendary legacy.
Zorbrak body types range from hulking to lithe, and their carapace can come in a wide range of hues from earthy to vibrant. They typically have a protruding, jagged maw and two sensory antennae, and they sometimes grow chitinous tendrils from their head.
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet
Homeworld: Vulx
As a Zorbrak, you have these special traits.
Climb Speed. You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.
Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Fearless. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition
Prey Stalker. You have proficiency in the Perception, Stealth, or Survival skill.
Scything Claws. You have a second pair of arms that end in sharp, blade-like claws that you can use to make Unarmed Strikes (Damage option only) with the Finesse property. On a hit, your claws deal 1d8 Slashing damage plus your ability modifier instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike. Additionally, if you have Advantage on an attack roll using your claws, it scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
Wraithform. As a Bonus Action, you magically gain the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn or until you make a damage roll or force someone to make a saving throw. When the Invisible condition on you from this trait ends, you treat Half Cover as Three-Quarters Cover until the end of your next turn. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Source: Outrunner’s Handbook

neon-odyssey/stardust-rhapsody.title: Stardust Rhapsody
neon-odyssey/stardust-rhapsody.content:
The Stardust Rhapsody is a singular galaxy shaped roughly like a vinyl record, filled with countless solar systems, worlds, and the space between. Also simply called the galaxy or reality, it serves as the analogue to D&D’s Material Plane on a much larger scale, with the cosmic realms serving as separate planes of existence. As far as anyone knows, there is only one galaxy in existence and there are no neighboring galaxies to travel to.
This setting is one of Space Opera, and while there are numerous elements from the broad science fiction umbrella, it is not the intention of Neon Odyssey to be concerned with real world science at all. There is no attempt to justify how anything works scientifically, and we have very deliberately stayed away from any influences of hard science fiction. Game Masters are encouraged to swiftly shut down any debates about scientific functioning that may arise at the table and slow down gameplay.
Worlds
Factions
Realms of the Cosmos

neon-odyssey/suns,-stars,-and-planets.title: Suns, Stars, and Planets
neon-odyssey/suns,-stars,-and-planets.content:
An important facet of this setting is that suns and stars are distinct and not the same concept. Suns are great balls of cosmic radiance that sit at the center of a solar system and give off the lifegiving heat and light, and are said to be the hatcheries of the grand solar phoenixes that fly throughout the cosmos. Stars, however, are a godly brilliance contained in the divine realm of Agathos that surrounds the galaxy, with positions that never change. This allows for relatively easy navigation by the stars no matter where you are in the galaxy.
There are a near-infinite number of planets, planetoids, and other celestial bodies throughout the Stardust Rhapsody, but the only ones capable of developing traditional life are those with a world soul, which are semi-sapient primordial entities of vast elemental power that dwell in a planetary core and dictate a world’s biome, flora, fauna, and temperament. Due to the rhythmic spinning of the galaxy like that of a record, every standard habitable world shares the same time signature, granting it the same rotational days, months, and years.
That said, there are plenty of strange, alien, and often undiscovered planets where non-traditional existence has cropped up with bizarre day/night cycles, year lengths, and gravitational effects that may lead to totally bizarre environments to explore and lifeforms to encounter. These planets often move throughout the galaxy indiscriminately and are difficult to navigate to, leading to numerous opportunities for skilled explorers, especially if rare and potent resources can be gathered or critical discoveries to be made.
Setting Primer

neon-odyssey/technology-and-economy.title: Technology and Economy
neon-odyssey/technology-and-economy.content:
The moment the song of creation was sung, the digital realm of the Hypergrid was created, and technology became possible by all of the galaxy’s inhabitants. This means that all worlds and civilizations have access to advanced technology and space travel. While some communities may favor less technological lifestyles, they all have equal access to travel the stars or harness the advancements that make life easier through technology.
Similarly, outside of a rare few instances, the entire galaxy shares the same economy and currency: the Galactic Note, denoted with the $ symbol. This currency is available in both digital and physical forms with a connection to the Hypergrid that keeps its value consistent across worlds and sectors. Most of the galactic economy flows through the financial wing of the Nexus Consortium, and broader galactic culture is one of consumerism and excess, with most everyday people seeking more notes, as it is not cheap to live in the Stardust Rhapsody.
For a quick conversion to D&D currency, one Gold Piece is equivalent to 50 Galactic Notes and the pricing of most standard items are roughly equivalent to the value of the US Dollar in 1997.
Setting Primer

neon-odyssey/the-eldest.title: The Eldest
neon-odyssey/the-eldest.content:
In this setting, the universe is a song. The Stardust Rhapsody was created by an impossibly ancient species of fish-like creatures known only as the Eldest. It is said that they existed in the deep, dark, quiet of the Abyssal Void before they joined together to sing the song of creation. In this moment, the galaxy, everything in it, and even the gods were sung into existence, and that song continues today. As far as most know, the Eldest are long extinct, with only far-flung ruins of their lost civilizations in the most remote reaches of the galaxy.
Setting Primer

neon-odyssey/worlds/adonia.title: Adonia
neon-odyssey/worlds/adonia.content:
An idyllic world that was once consumed by a sun and remade by Alara the Lightbringer. Sun-soaked valleys with a strong presence of solar phoenixes. Homeworld of the solari and capital of the Solar Federation.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/astrovega.title: Astrovega
neon-odyssey/worlds/astrovega.content:
A world of duality, with half of the planet covered in oceans, coastlines, and highly advanced cities and the other half covered in ruined wastelands due to technological experimentation. Homeworld of the laika. Founding hub of the Argonauts. Member of the Solar Federation.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/bortuun.title: Bortuun
neon-odyssey/worlds/bortuun.content:
An icy planet of tundras, snowy mountains, frozen seas, and great auroras said to provide prophecy and strange things frozen in the ice. Caverns and hidden valleys of lush forests and jungles are hidden by mist. Homeworld of the yaungu. World of the Empire.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/cabaret.title: Cabaret
neon-odyssey/worlds/cabaret.content:
A world fully corrupted by the Discordant tone of Thrill, with strange tent cities, false landscapes, a springy ring station, and other areas where the party never ends. Home to many motliens.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/caldoa.title: Caldoa
neon-odyssey/worlds/caldoa.content:
A highly volcanic planet with regions of oppressive lava and great stretches of lushness amidst churning seas. Homeworld of the volcar and a landing point of the Void Dominium.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/cicero-prime.title: Cicero Prime
neon-odyssey/worlds/cicero-prime.content:
A war-torn world besieged by the Discordant tone of Instinct, where a final bastion of humanity fights for survival and democracy against endless hives of bug-like fiends. Home to many dathu.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/ferrox.title: Ferrox
neon-odyssey/worlds/ferrox.content:
A world covered in an enormous junkyard where rampant rust storms prevent atmospheric flight, with the rugged populace roving in caravans of ramshackle ground vehicles. Also serves as a prison for galactic criminals. A hub of the Chemtek Revolution.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/goro.title: Goro
neon-odyssey/worlds/goro.content:
A storming world where tempests rage across violent seas, rugged mountains, tall forests, hostile battlefields, and neon-soaked megacities. Homeworld of the raizo and clawderan. Headquarters of the Kuzai Syndicate.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/k'thar.title: K'Thar
neon-odyssey/worlds/k'thar.content:
One of the oldest planets covered in Eldest ruins and the wreckage of civilizations who tried and failed to survive the harsh spires and black seas. Homeworld of the yoggoth. A hub of the Polaris Society.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/kharabis.title: Kharabis
neon-odyssey/worlds/kharabis.content:
A world covered in ocean with numerous islands above great reefs and the dark depths below filled with leviathans. Homeworld of the jozza and murexians. Founding hub of the Church of Karkosa. Member of the Solar Federation.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/krayta.title: Krayta
neon-odyssey/worlds/krayta.content:
A world of primeval landscapes including primordial jungles, towering volcanoes, and archaic seas, heavily populated by dinosaurs. Homeworld of the saurians and tekal and capital of the Saurok Dynasty.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/lythora.title: Lythora
neon-odyssey/worlds/lythora.content:
A world made of gemstone and crystal, particularly harmonyte with a very strong connection to the Harmony and the kindred entities within. A seat of the Saurok Dynasty.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/mavros.title: Mavros
neon-odyssey/worlds/mavros.content:
A red planet that surges with psionic energy and covered in dusty badlands and alien flora and fauna. Homeworld of the zeticulans and marsoom, it also serves as a neutral zone of galactic politics.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/megadyne.title: Megadyne
neon-odyssey/worlds/megadyne.content:
An entirely mechanical planet with a synthetic world soul downloaded from the Hypergrid, populated by mostly robots with invasions from the Discordant tone of Progress. Homeworld of the anitrons, with many isotrons and terminox.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/morzebe.title: Morzebe
neon-odyssey/worlds/morzebe.content:
An acidic world where the surface is irradiated wasteland swarming with mutants and monsters, with grand subterranean caverns housing a thriving civilization of mechs and military. Homeworld of the oculok.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/neo-edifex.title: Neo-Edifex
neon-odyssey/worlds/neo-edifex.content:
A world completely covered by a single enormous megacity that is split into two levels with a highly advanced metropolis above and a gritty undercity below. Headquarters of the Nexus Consortium and a hub of the Chemtek Revolution. Member of the Solar Federation.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/noxilus.title: Noxilus
neon-odyssey/worlds/noxilus.content:
A planet of endless night fully corrupted by the Discordant tone of Entropy, where undead creatures roam the rugged highlands between sleek cities where the galactic underbelly thrives. Home to many varg.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/polygonia.title: Polygonia
neon-odyssey/worlds/polygonia.content:
A whimsical world heavily changed by the realm of Arcadia, with environments of video game biomes that defy reason, shifting temples of lost artifacts, and many arcade fey. Homeworld of the navili with many bitlings.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/prismara.title: Prismara
neon-odyssey/worlds/prismara.content:
The ultimate tourism world with a prismatic sky over deserts and mountains filled with cities of casinos and entertainment and picturesque tropical seas with beautiful beaches. Homeworld of the glowblins, poggles, and flambego.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/sethreen.title: Sethreen
neon-odyssey/worlds/sethreen.content:
A verdant and deadly world overgrown with poisonous plants and teeming venomous creatures, with beautiful jungles, marshes of giant mushrooms, and deserts dotted with cactus forests. Homeworld of the gorgonites, amanites, and pakku. Member of the Solar Federation.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/shensaati.title: Shensaati
neon-odyssey/worlds/shensaati.content:
A world entirely covered in deserts and arid mountains. It has a mystical connection to the flow of time, called the Golden Dial, with many temporal anomalies. Homeworld of the zamani. World of the Cavalon Empire.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/sleema.title: Sleema
neon-odyssey/worlds/sleema.content:
A planet covered in putrid swamps, choking bogs, and treacherous marshes filled with exotic food ingredients sold in great market cities with towers for space transports. Homeworld of the nematoans and greebles. World of the Cavalon Empire.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/tibbulus.title: Tibbulus
neon-odyssey/worlds/tibbulus.content:
A mostly gaseous world with a windy surface of fluffy clouds and floating cities, and great seas of gelatinous ooze beneath the cloud cover where pipe settlements thrive. Homeworld of the oozoids and zephursa. World of the Cavalon Empire.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/titan-ix.title: Titan IX
neon-odyssey/worlds/titan-ix.content:
A colossal space station the size of a small world built around one of the first aether asteroids, filled with rigid structure, military might, and scientific advancements. Home colony of the aetheron and rangor. Headquarters of the Grimnir Company.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/uthen.title: Uthen
neon-odyssey/worlds/uthen.content:
A pastoral world with rolling hills, fertile farmland, dense forests, craggy highlands, and towering mountains. Treacherous lairs of giants, dragons, and other monsters lurk in its remote reaches. Capital of the Cavalon Empire.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/uulzoth.title: Uulzoth
neon-odyssey/worlds/uulzoth.content:
The first world of the galaxy, said to be where the Eldest first sang the song of creation, thought by most to be lost. A place covered in ruined Eldest cities, subterranean seas, and mind-shattering dreams. Hidden by the light at the center of the galaxy, as well as warped time and space.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/val'shai.title: Val'Shai
neon-odyssey/worlds/val'shai.content:
A shattered world in the Wyrmways heavily changed after it was ripped from the galaxy through a black hole. Covered in void coral and serves as the primary breeding ground for void wyrms. Homeworld of the benthos and nilari.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/viridar.title: Viridar
neon-odyssey/worlds/viridar.content:
A heavily forested world with alpine mountains and grand rivers, surging with savage energies that affect the planet’s beasts and dinosaurs. A seat of power of the Saurok Dynasty and is stripped for resources and polluted by the Nexus Consortium.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/vulx.title: Vulx
neon-odyssey/worlds/vulx.content:
A haunted world with an undead world soul after the planet was killed in a necromantic ritual. Covered in huge dead forests, needle-like mountains, and vast boneyards and crawling with undead and monstrous behemoths. Homeworld of the skettik and zorbrak.
Worlds

neon-odyssey/worlds/index.content:

neon-odyssey/worlds/zartoga.content:
A moon-sized space port built from the wreckages of thousands of ships scrapped together into a haven for pirates and other outlaws at the center of a treacherous plasma storm. Headquarters of the Bloodfleet.

neon-odyssey/index.title: Neon Odyssey
neon-odyssey/index.content:
About
Neon Odyssey is a 1,400+ page trilogy that brings Space Opera to D&D 5.5e, drawing inspiration from legendary Sci-Fi Films, retro Video Games, classic Animation, pop-culture Nostalgia, and more, written and published by the creators of The Crooked Moon. Launch into a space adventure with galactic GM Tools in a colorfully cosmic Campaign Setting, or suit up with an astral arsenal of Player Options to soar among the stars.
This site contains useful notes about the Stardust Rhapsody and the mechanics of Neon Odyssey. It will also include helpful notes regarding any upcoming one-shots or campaigns set in the Stardust Rhapsody.
Backerkit
The full trilogy is expected to ship at the end of 2027. Pre-Orders are available via Backerkit.
